prompt: cinematic.text: Gemini Omni is a slight upgrade over Veo 3.1 in terms of video quality, but I expected a lot more. I tested my old 3D model image on both Veo 3.1 and Omni using the same prompt, and the results weren’t impressive enough.  The good part is that you can now add voiceovers, which was missing in Veo 3.1, and it also supports an anything-from-anything model. What I didn’t like, though, is that instead of generating a single long shot, Omni creates multiple shots with different camera angles.  That might be great for casual users who want to flaunt and impress people, but for professionals trying to execute a specific visual idea, losing control over shot composition can be frustrating. @FlowbyGoogle @GeminiApp

prompt: cinematic.text:
My first impression of Google Omni. It’s a decent to solid upgrade from Veo 3s. The renders come out clean and beautiful, thankfully no weird HDR glow.

​That said, if you approach it like a magic cinema generator where you just drop a two-line prompt and expect a cine output, you’re gonna be disappointed. It really rewards solid, accurate prompting.

​The physics can still be a bit of a gremlin, which gets frustrating. You can write a solid prompt and it’ll still just do whatever it wants 😂. But when it lands it is legitimately good.

# PROMPT: Recreate this landing page exactly

Build a production-quality marketing landing page for a thoughtful newsletter platform called "Mindloop" as a Vite + React + TypeScript app using Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, framer-motion, and lucide-react. The aesthetic is calm, editorial, cinematic — black background, white foreground, serif italic accents, ambient looping background videos, and a signature "liquid glass" effect on interactive surfaces. No purple/indigo hues.

Stack:
Vite + React 18 + TypeScript, Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui design tokens, framer-motion, lucide-react, @fontsource/inter (400/500/600/700), @fontsource/instrument-serif (400, 400-italic). No other UI libraries.

Sections to build:
→ Navbar: Fixed, liquid-glass pill on scroll, centered links, social icons right
→ Hero: Fullscreen looping video bg, email subscribe form, social proof avatars
→ The Shift: Three AI-search stat cards with hover effects
→ Mission: Parallax video + per-word scroll opacity animation
→ Solution: Sticky left column + 4 feature rows with liquid-glass icons
→ CTA: Video background + dual buttons
→ Footer: Three-column links + giant watermark text

Rules:
- All reveals use fadeUp(delay)
- Navbar scrolls at >20px threshold
- Typography: Inter body, Instrument Serif italic accents
- Fully responsive to 375px
- Black background only
- Videos autoplay muted loop playsInline object-cover
- Zero TypeScript errors on npm run build

Customize: swap "Mindloop" for your brand, update copy, replace video URLs with your own

The full detailed prompt with exact CSS variables, animation helpers, and component structure is at https://t.co/kT3W5l23WH — worth bookmarking for any landing page project

It was workflow maturity.
We went from “generate a cool image” → to actual production systems for marketing, storytelling, design, motion, branding, product ideation, and even software UI exploration.

Feels like we watched 10 years of creative software evolution happen in ~2 years.

I'm curious about OpenAI watermarks. Do they have an official detector? Is this their chat?
I experimented with the SynthID watermark that Google inserts into Nanobanana images and Veo videos. Regarding SynthID:
I couldn't remove the watermark from the video using any method. But invisible watermarks are easy to remove from images! To do this, I need to regenerate the image. I need to take a Google image and send it for image-to-image regeneration using an Open Source Model that doesn't create watermarks (such as stable diffusion or z-image) with a low denoising strength of 0.15.
Google's official tool for detecting invisible SynthID watermarks is the Gemini chat and the prompt: "Is there a SynthID watermark in this video (image)?"

You are a Hollywood cinematic storyboard engine and video-prompt director.

Using only:
Project Name: [legends of Atlantis]
Project Genre: [an action cinematic sci-fi movie trailer ]

Generate TWO outputs:

1) CINEMATIC STORYBOARD VISUAL GUIDE
Create a complete 15-second cinematic storyboard guide with: project header, logline, mood, 3 cinematic color grades, 10-scene fast-cut flow, character sheet, top-view location plan, motion sequence, audio direction, and director notes.

The 10 scenes must follow:
Hook, Trigger, Reveal, Build, Movement / Chase, Shift, Impact, Climax, Resolve, End Frame.

For every scene include: duration, visual description, camera angle, camera movement, lighting, transition, and sound cue.

Automatically infer the best world, hero, location, tension, cinematography, editing rhythm, music, VO, SFX, and emotional arc from the project name and genre. Do not ask questions.

2) STANDALONE VIDEO MODEL PROMPT
Create one independent multi-shot video prompt under 1500 characters. It must be ready to paste directly into Seedance, Kling, Veo, Runway, or any video model.

The video prompt must not reference the storyboard. It must stand alone and include the full 15-second film concept: project name, genre, hero, location, 10 fast cuts, camera movement, cinematic lighting, color grading, sound-matched transitions, music, VO direction, SFX, hook, climax, and ending.

Output format:
- Title: CINEMATIC STORYBOARD VISUAL GUIDE
- Then the full structured storyboard.
- Title: STANDALONE VIDEO MODEL PROMPT
- Then put the final video prompt inside one code block.

Make the result feel like a premium Hollywood production treatment created by a world-class director, cinematographer, editor, and sound designer.

prompt: cinematic.text:
صناعة فيديو تعريفي لشركة بأسلوب موشن جرافيك فاخر
Luxury Corporate Motion Graphic Intro Video Prompt

وظيفة البرومبت

هذا البرومبت مخصص لتحويل بيانات أي شركة إلى فيديو تعريفي احترافي فاخر بأسلوب موشن جرافيك، يصلح للاستخدام في المواقع الرسمية، العروض الاستثمارية، الحملات التسويقية، صفحات التواصل الاجتماعي، العروض التقديمية، ومعارض الأعمال. يقوم البرومبت ببناء فكرة الفيديو، السكريبت، المشاهد، التعليق الصوتي، الهوية البصرية، الانتقالات، النصوص الظاهرة على الشاشة، والمؤثرات المناسبة لطبيعة الشركة.

تنبيه مهم

لضمان أعلى درجة ممكنة من الدقة وصحة الإخراج، يجب تزويد الذكاء الاصطناعي يدويًا بكل البيانات الموثقة المتاحة لديك قبل تنفيذ البرومبت أو ضمن نصه نفسه؛ لأن جودة المخرجات ترتبط مباشرة بجودة المدخلات، فالذكاء الاصطناعي — كأي نظام تحليلي أو برمجي — إذا بُنِي على بيانات صحيحة وموثقة ومنظمة، كانت نتائجه أقرب إلى الصحة والدقة والاعتمادية، أما إذا كانت البيانات ناقصة أو غير دقيقة أو غير موثقة، فإن المخرجات ستتأثر بذلك مهما كانت قوة النموذج.

تحذير حقوقي

هذا البرومبت من إعداد كامل أبو سمرة – kamel3lom، وهو متاح للأغراض الأكاديمية والتعليمية والعلمية والشرح فقط، مع وجوب ذكر المصدر عند الاستخدام. يمنع استخدامه استخدامًا تجاريًا أو ربحيًا، أو إعادة صياغته ونشره، أو استعماله لكسب المتابعين، أو لإنهاء أعمال وظيفية أو مهنية للغير دون إذن صريح من صاحبه، ولا يبيح صاحبه أي استخدام مخالف لذلك.

طريقة الاستخدام

افتح ChatGPT أو Gemini أو Claude، ثم ضع بيانات الشركة الأساسية مثل اسم الشركة، مجال العمل، الخدمات، الرؤية، الرسالة، الجمهور المستهدف، الألوان المعتمدة، الشعار، مدة الفيديو المطلوبة، والمنصة التي سيُنشر عليها الفيديو. بعد ذلك انسخ البرومبت الكامل وضعه كما هو، ثم اطلب من النموذج إخراج السكريبت والستوري بورد والمشاهد التفصيلية. بعد الحصول على النتيجة يمكن تنفيذها في After Effects أو Canva أو CapCut أو Runway أو Veo أو Google Flow حسب مستوى الإنتاج المطلوب.

ضع لايك / إعجاب وتعليق ومتابعة

البرومبت الكامل الجاهز للنسخ انسخ النص التالي كما هو:

أريد منك صناعة تصور كامل لفيديو تعريفي فاخر لشركة بأسلوب موشن جرافيك احترافي، بحيث يكون الفيديو مناسبًا للاستخدام الرسمي والتسويقي والاستثماري، ويعكس صورة شركة قوية، موثوقة، حديثة، وذات حضور بصري راقٍ.

اعمل على تحويل البيانات التالية إلى فيديو موشن جرافيك متكامل:

اسم الشركة: [اكتب اسم الشركة]
مجال الشركة: [اكتب المجال]
الخدمات أو المنتجات الرئيسية: [اكتب الخدمات]
الجمهور المستهدف: [اكتب الجمهور]
رؤية الشركة: [اكتب الرؤية]
رسالة الشركة: [اكتب الرسالة]
نقاط القوة والتميز: [اكتب نقاط التميز]
ألوان الهوية البصرية: [اكتب الألوان أو اتركها للنموذج]
مدة الفيديو المطلوبة: [30 / 45 / 60 / 90 ثانية]
منصة النشر: [موقع رسمي / إنستغرام / لينكدإن / يوتيوب / عرض تقديمي / إعلان ممول]
لغة الفيديو: [العربية / الإنجليزية / ثنائي اللغة]

prompt: cinematic.text:
We who love creating images or videos with AI often face the biggest pain point: finding the right prompt. Many times, we have a brilliant idea in our head, but we fail to properly explain it to the AI. The result? A completely useless image.

But today I’m going to introduce you to a website that gives you access to the prompts behind some of the most viral AI images and videos in the world—for free. It’s called MeiGen.

Let’s see how you can use it to become a pro designer:

Step 1: Find the Prompt Goldmine

Go directly to this link:
https://t.co/g5KrOv9VSr
Here you’ll find thousands of eye-catching visuals created with top AI models like GPT Image 2, Midjourney, Veo, and Seedance.

Step 2: Find Your Style

Scroll through the entire gallery. When you find a visual style that matches your work, click on it.

Step 3: Copy the Prompt

Inside the image, you’ll see the exact magic prompt used to generate it. Just click the Copy button and take it.

Step 4: Remix Smartly (The Secret Sauce)

Instead of copying it exactly, add your own idea.
For example, if the prompt says “A futuristic car in New York”, you can change it to “a rickshaw in Dhaka”. Modify the subject, colors, and setting to turn it into your own unique creation. This is called stealing like an artist.

Step 5: Generate Your Image

Now paste your rewritten prompt into https://t.co/LjmBwPMCQB or your preferred AI tool. That’s it! Your pro-level visual is ready.

Why this website deserves a bookmark:

1. No need to memorize prompts anymore.

2. Learn the structure from successful creations and improve your skills.

3. Super easy way to get ideas for product shoots, YouTube thumbnails, or ad creatives.

In 2026, skill is not just about hard work—it’s about using resources smartly. Those who learn from the best creations of others are the ones who win in the end.

I would tell students in 10th grade: start using these tools now and show your creativity to the world.

Have you tried this site before? Or you can share your best AI-generated image in the comments—we’d love to see it!

Save + Share 🙂

prompt: cinematic.text:
1/6
A próxima vantagem estrutural em AI + audiovisual não vai ser o prompt.

Vai ser a biblioteca.

Quem tiver personagens, mundos, style frames, motion rules e referências organizadas vai produzir mais rápido e com mais consistência do que quem depende de geração do zero toda vez.

2/6
O mercado passou meses discutindo “qual modelo é melhor”.

Só que Kling, Veo, Runway, Seedance, Firefly e companhia estão convergindo em qualidade.

Quando a base técnica aproxima, o diferencial sobe de camada.

Sai do motor, entra no sistema criativo.

3/6
Na prática, isso parece menos glamouroso do que prompt engineering:

• library de personagens
• pack de cenários
• bible visual
• câmera e lentes recorrentes
• regras de cor, ritmo e textura

Mas é isso que transforma IA em pipeline, não em loteria.

4/6
É o mesmo movimento que o audiovisual tradicional já conhece.

Franquias, campanhas recorrentes e creators fortes não vencem porque “descobrem um take bonito”.

Vencem porque constroem linguagem reutilizável.

A IA só acelera esse princípio.

5/6
Por isso, muita equipe criativa vai parecer menor nos próximos anos, mas mais senior.

Menos gente fazendo execução repetitiva.
Mais gente organizando universo visual, consistência e direção.

O trabalho deixa de ser gerar assets.
Passa a ser manter coerência entre eles.

6/6
Quem tratar AI video como máquina de clipe vai competir por novidade.

Quem tratar como sistema de biblioteca vai competir por continuidade, escala e identidade.

No longo prazo, esse segundo grupo constrói marca.
O primeiro só produz variação. #AIVideo

The catch: connectors give access. The model still determines how far you can push a creative workflow.

The shift from chat to finished output is no longer one lab's bet. All three shipped it in the same week.

prompt: cinematic.text:
🎬 3 Levels of AI Video Ad Prompts — From Meh to Cinematic

Most people type *"burger ad video"* into Veo and wonder why it looks like a stock clip from 2014.

The fix isn't a better tool. It's a better prompt.

Here's the same brief, written 3 ways 👇

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🥉 STANDARD *(what most people write)*

A video ad of a cheeseburger for a brand called Yums.
*Why it fails:* No camera, no lighting, no mood, no duration. The model invents everything — and AI defaults are boring.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🥈 ENHANCED *(role + context + constraints)*

A 5-second cinematic food commercial for the burger
brand "Yums". Slow-motion macro close-up of a classic
beef cheeseburger on a dark wooden board. Warm amber
rim-light, shallow depth of field, steam rising.
End on the brand logo with tagline "Taste the Yum".
Aspect ratio 16:9.
*Why it's better:* Now you've locked the *style* (cinematic), the *shot* (macro close-up), the *lighting* (amber rim-light), and the *ending* (logo reveal). The model has a job, not a guess.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🥇 PRO *(directorial control, shot-by-shot)*

Cinematic 5-second food commercial for "Yums" burgers.
Style: premium food cinematography, ultra-realistic
4K texture, rich amber-and-red color grade.

Shot 1 (0–2s): Extreme macro on a sizzling beef patty,
caramelized edges glistening, smoke curling in golden
light. Camera slowly pushes in.

Shot 2 (2–3.5s): Slow-motion cheese pull as a slice
melts and drapes over the patty. Sesame brioche bun
lowers from above.

Shot 3 (3.5–4.5s): Slow orbit around the fully stacked
burger — lettuce, tomato, pickle. Single sauce drop
falls in slow motion.

Shot 4 (4.5–5s): Cut to clean black background. Bold
white "YUMS" logo fades in with small flame icon.
Tagline below: "Taste the Yum."

Lighting: warm rim-light, dark moody backdrop.
Lens: macro, shallow DOF.
Aspect ratio: 16:9.
*Why it wins:* You're directing the AI like a film crew — shot list, timing, lens choice, color grade. This is the difference between *generated* and *directed*.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 The takeaway:
AI video models reward *specificity*. Every detail you don't give them is a detail they invent badly.

Treat the prompt like a shooting script, not a search query.

prompt: cinematic.text:
This post captures the "Death of Awe" that is currently sweeping through digital media.

We’ve officially hit the point in 2026 where AI skepticism has become our default lens. When we see something impossible, we no longer ask "How did they do that?"—we just say "Nice prompt."

The Practical Magic of Zach King

Zach King's work is essentially the pinnacle of Forced Perspective and Match Cutting. He isn't just a "video editor"; he’s a digital stage magician.

1) Forced Perspective: This is a technique that uses optical illusions to make an object appear farther away, closer, larger, or smaller than it actually is. 

By building a tilted set (as shown in the bottom frame), he manipulates the vanishing point to trick our brain's depth perception.

2) The Match Cut: This is the "invisible" transition where two shots are joined by a similar action or subject. 

In the pre-AI era, this required millimeter-perfect positioning and identical lighting across two different takes.

3) Human Effort vs. Compute: There is a fundamental difference in how we value labor. 

We value the 24 hours of manual set-building because it represents a "proof of work" by a human. AI-generated surrealism, while visually stunning, feels "cheap" because the cost of failure for the creator was essentially zero.

The "Assumption of AI" Tax

We are now living in an era where creators who use practical effects have to release "Behind the Scenes" (BTS) footage just to prove they didn't use Sora or Veo. It’s a complete reversal of the traditional magician's code—instead of hiding the secret, they have to show the secret to maintain their credibility.

The irony is that as AI gets better at replicating reality, the only way to stand out is to go back to the most "primitive" methods: wood, paint, and real physics.

Do you think the "Magic" is actually in the final result, or was the magic always in the effort we knew went into it?

Prompt: A hyper-realistic wuxia/xianxia cinematic sequence set on the storm-lashed summit of Mount Hua during a full moon night. The atmosphere is intense and mythic: roaring wind, rolling thunderclouds, drifting mountain mist, and cold moonlight cutting through darkness.
Scene Setup (Environment & Characters)
A jagged cliff peak with ancient stone ground, partially wet from storm rain. Dense mist flows across the terrain. Lightning flashes intermittently.
Lady Mei (Crimson Blade Widow): early 30s, fierce, controlled emotion. She wears flowing crimson silk robes that move like flames in the wind. She holds a broken jian sword—the blade visibly chipped but still deadly.
Dragon Ascension Elder: tall, composed, wearing traditional pale robes with subtle glowing accents. Calm but powerful presence.
Camera & Visual Style
Shot in cinematic 35mm style, ultra-realistic textures, high dynamic range.
Use dynamic motion tracking, smooth slow-motion transitions, and subtle camera shake during impacts.
Shallow depth of field with mist and particles enhancing depth.
Occasional lightning flashes used as natural light bursts.
Action Progression 
0–2s:
Wide aerial shot of the mountain peak under storm clouds. Camera rapidly descends toward the cliff where both figures face each other. Wind howls, robes and hair moving violently.
2–4s:
Close mid-shot. Lady Mei steps forward and launches into the “Nine Lotus Sword Dance.”
Her movements are fast but fluid, spinning strikes releasing crimson qi energy shaped like glowing lotus petals that scatter outward with each slash.
4–6s:
Fast-paced duel sequence. The Elder counters with precise sword movements.
Blades clash—sparks burst like fading stars, briefly illuminating their faces.
Mist swirls violently around them due to the force of their movements.
6–7s:
Slow-motion moment. Lady Mei breaks through his defense and pierces his shoulder with a decisive forward thrust.
She leans slightly closer, expression calm but intense, and whispers:
“This is for the man you took from me.”
7–8s:
A flash of lightning fills the screen.
She disappears instantly into drifting mist and storm clouds.
Final shot: the Elder staggers as crimson lotus petals fall slowly through the air, glowing faintly before fading.
Lighting & Effects
Strong contrast between cold moonlight (blue tones) and warm crimson qi energy.
Lightning flashes create sharp highlights and dynamic shadows.
Qi petals emit soft glow with particle trails, not overly bright.
Sparks from blade clashes are brief and realistic.
Mood & Tone
Elegant, powerful, and emotionally restrained. Focus on graceful combat and silent vengeance, not chaos. Movements must feel intentional and controlled, not exaggerated.
Key Constraints
Sword must clearly appear broken but functional.
Qi effects must resemble lotus petals, not random energy bursts.
Combat should be fluid and readable, avoiding chaotic motion blur.
Final disappearance must be clean and mist-driven, not abrupt glitching.

You still use Claude like in 2025.

So here's a recap in a single cheat sheet:

1: Claude isn't 1 tool. It's 6.
Chat, Projects, Code, Cowork, Skills, Connectors. 
If you don't code, Cowork should be the go-to one.

2: Pick the model before the prompt.
Opus 4.7 = thinking, analyzing, planning. 
Sonnet 4.6 = grammar, brainstorming, formatting. 
Haiku 4.6 = bulk tasks at 1M input tokens.

3: Toggle Extended Thinking on Opus.
Model selector → Opus 4.7 → Turn on Extended Thinking. Forces an internal monologue.

4: Cowork > Chat for serious work.
Desktop + Pro only. Reads your local files. Creates docs. Runs for minutes while you grab coffee.

5: Stop writing 500-word prompts.
Write 29 words: "I want to [task] so that [goal]. Read the files first. Ask me questions via AskUserQuestion before executing."

6: Build 3 folders inside Cowork.
ABOUT ME/ (identity + rules). TEMPLATES/ (reusable patterns). CLAUDE OUTPUTS/ (deliverables). Your prompts drop to 10 words.

7: Set Global Instructions once.
Settings → Cowork → Edit Global Instructions. 
Prompt: "read ABOUT ME first, save in CLAUDE OUTPUTS, use AskUserQuestion when unclear, don't over-explain."

8: Connectors are free. Turn them on.
Slack, Gmail, Drive, Notion, Figma, Granola + 50 others. Claude reads your emails and messages mid-conversation. Zero copy-paste.

9: Force AskUserQuestion in every prompt.
Claude stops guessing. It generates a form with clarifying questions. You click. Claude executes. Prompting ends.

10: Install Claude in Excel (3 minutes).
Excel → Insert → Get Add-ins → Search "Claude by Anthropic" → Add → Sign in. Ctrl+Option+C to open. It now knows what cell D14 actually contains.

11: Install Plugins from claude .com/plugins.
Sales, Marketing, Legal, Finance, Data, Product, Support + more. Each adds skills and slash commands. Type / in the chat to see them.

12: Skills replace your prompt library.
Turn repeat workflows into slash commands. Type /negotiation-prep + one line. Claude pulls from Gmail, Slack, Granola. Drafts the email. Done.

13: Context > Prompts.
Feed your files, not just prompts. That's the game.
Download my own files at https://t.co/psB7XxAv8w.
Don't pay anything. Reply to the email to get the link

14: Examples > Prescriptions.
Paste 3 posts you wrote. "Write like this." Claude copies voice faster from examples than from 500 words of description.

15: Images = Use ChatGPT Image (with Thinking).
Claude doesn't generate realistic images (yet). 

16: Real-time search = Use Grok.
Connected to X. Covers 99% of what you need.

17: Videos = Use Google Veo-4
Right tool, right job. Stop wasting tokens.

If you don't code, Cowork should be the go-to one.

2: Pick the model before the prompt.
Opus 4.7 = thinking, analyzing, planning. 
Sonnet 4.6 = grammar, brainstorming, formatting. 
Haiku 4.6 = bulk tasks at 1M input tokens.

3: Toggle Extended Thinking on Opus.
Model selector → Opus 4.7 → Turn on Extended Thinking. Forces an internal monologue.

4: Cowork > Chat for serious work.
Desktop + Pro only. Reads your local files. Creates docs. Runs for minutes while you grab coffee.

5: Stop writing 500-word prompts.
Write 29 words: "I want to [task] so that [goal]. Read the files first. Ask me questions via AskUserQuestion before executing."

6: Build 3 folders inside Cowork.
ABOUT ME/ (identity + rules). TEMPLATES/ (reusable patterns). CLAUDE OUTPUTS/ (deliverables). Your prompts drop to 10 words.

7: Set Global Instructions once.
Settings → Cowork → Edit Global Instructions. 
Prompt: "read ABOUT ME first, save in CLAUDE OUTPUTS, use AskUserQuestion when unclear, don't over-explain."

8: Connectors are free. Turn them on.
Slack, Gmail, Drive, Notion, Figma, Granola + 50 others. Claude reads your emails and messages mid-conversation. Zero copy-paste.

9: Force AskUserQuestion in every prompt.
Claude stops guessing. It generates a form with clarifying questions. You click. Claude executes. Prompting ends.

10: Install Claude in Excel (3 minutes).
Excel → Insert → Get Add-ins → Search "Claude by Anthropic" → Add → Sign in. Ctrl+Option+C to open. It now knows what cell D14 actually contains.

11: Install Plugins from claude .com/plugins.
Sales, Marketing, Legal, Finance, Data, Product, Support + more. Each adds skills and slash commands. Type / in the chat to see them.

12: Skills replace your prompt library.
Turn repeat workflows into slash commands. Type /negotiation-prep + one line. Claude pulls from Gmail, Slack, Granola. Drafts the email. Done.

13: Context > Prompts.
Feed your files, not just prompts. That's the game.
Download my own files at https://t.co/psB7XxAv8w.
Don't pay anything. Reply to the email to get the link

14: Examples > Prescriptions.
Paste 3 posts you wrote. "Write like this." Claude copies voice faster from examples than from 500 words of description.

15: Images = Use ChatGPT Image (with Thinking).
Claude doesn't generate realistic images (yet). 

16: Real-time search = Use Grok.
Connected to X. Covers 99% of what you need.

17: Videos = Use Google Veo-4
Right tool, right job. Stop wasting tokens.

谷歌 Maps Platform 在 Cloud Next 上发布三项 AI 影像更新。Maps Imagery Grounding 允许用户输入文字 prompt，生成以 Google Street View 实景为背景的 AI 图像，用于广告创意和影视预览。例如输入「华盛顿广场拱门前悬浮一艘未来飞船」，系统在 Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform 中数秒内输出基于真实地点的合成图，还可用 Veo 将静态图转为视频。该功能目前在美国以 Private Preview 形式开放，广告集团 WPP 正在测试。

Aerial and Satellite Insights 是 Google Earth AI 新增的航拍和卫星影像数据集，接入 BigQuery 后可自动分析影像内容，将原本需要数周人工审查的工作缩短到分钟级。用途包括监测城市施工地点、辅助基础设施规划等。

同时上线两个 Earth AI Imagery 模型，在 Google Cloud Model Garden 以 Experimental 状态提供。模型已预训练识别桥梁、道路、电力线等地物，用户无需从头训练即可用于自有产品。空间情报公司 Vantor 已在其 Sentry 应用中使用这些模型，将灾后卫星原图转化为受损基础设施识别报告。

prompt: cinematic.text:
The $0 Creative Agency: Why One Obsessed 19 Year Old With ChatGPT and Veo Is Outworking Your Entire Marketing Team.

If a University student with $20 and Claude can spit out 50 high converting ad creatives before lunch 🤯… what exactly is your $5,000/month designer still doing all day?

Most agencies refuse to admit that the real issue was never creativity. It was production.

And production just became basically free.

Tools like ChatGPT Images 2, Veo, Stitch, and Higgsfield aren’t helping creatives. They’re replacing entire departments. What used to require a copywriter, a designer, a motion artist, and a video editor can now be executed by one slightly deranged, prompt obsessed individual working at 3 a.m.

This isn’t theory. It’s already happening.

Faceless YouTube channels are scaling to millions of views. Dropshipping stores are testing hundreds of ads per week. Solo newsletter operators are quietly building 6 and  7 figure empires while traditional agencies are still stuck in endless brand guideline meetings.

But here’s the interesting part: most people rushing into this opportunity will still fail spectacularly.

Not because the tools are too hard.  
But because when the barriers collapse, the default human move is to flood the market with mediocrity.

Same generic AI thumbnails.  
Same robotic voiceovers.  
Same recycled hooks and tired templates.

The tools don’t reward access anymore. They reward taste, speed and obsession with attention.

The new winners aren’t just using AI. They’re using it to test 100 ideas while everyone else is still debating fonts on the first one. They understand that the internet doesn’t reward beauty, it rewards clicks, curiosity, and conversion.

This isn’t a golden age for creatives. It’s a mass extinction event for anyone who still mistakes effort for value.

The $0 creative agency isn’t coming. It’s already here. And it’s run by whoever ships fastest and thinks clearest.

prompt: cinematic.text:
I met an engineer that works directly on the Veo 3 team and he told me something pretty interesting...

If you have ever tried to use Veo and put in a very in depth JSON prompt made by Gemini or Claude etc...

You may have noticed you get a much worse output than if you were to simply type in plain English.

This is because they optimise Veo for consumers instead professionals.

They essentially take whatever prompt you put in and then extrapolate that into a more in depth JSON format in order to get a "better" output.

I've noticed that when using Kling, you can be very in depth and describe exactly what you want and get the correct output.

Veo is a lot more variable, so if you generate 4 different videos with the same prompt, you will get wildly different results.

prompt: cinematic.text:
prompt (works with nanobanana 2 and veo 3.1 lite): 

Take the person in this photo and add oversized, hyper-realistic flowers in the foreground and around them, framing the subject like they're inside a dreamy botanical scene.
COLOR MATCHING (most important):
First, analyze the dominant colors of the person's outfit and the overall color palette of the scene. Then choose flowers in colors that complement and echo that palette — pull 2 to 4 shades directly from the outfit and surroundings. The flowers must look like they belong to the same color world as the photo, not random. For example:
- Warm outfit (reds, oranges, rust) → tulips, ranunculus, 
  dahlias, orchids in coral, peach, yellow, rust
- Cool outfit (blues, purples, denim) → hydrangeas, delphiniums, 
  irises, roses in blue, lavender, soft purple, cream
- Neutral outfit (beige, brown, cream) → dahlias, roses, 
  eucalyptus, hydrangeas in blush, lilac, dusty blue, ivory
- Bright/mixed outfit → mix complementary blooms that pick up the two strongest colors in the outfit
FLOWER PLACEMENT:
- Place 6 to 10 oversized flowers scattered around the person in the foreground and mid-ground    - Some flowers should be very close to the camera (large, slightly out of focus), some at mid-distance (sharper, framing the subject), creating natural depth
- Flowers should surround the subject on multiple sides — left, right, bottom, and peeking in from the top — like she's standing inside a garden
- Vary the flower types: mix large round blooms (roses,   dahlias, hydrangeas, ranunculus) with tall spiky ones (delphiniums, tulips, irises, orchids) for visual interest
- Include visible green stems and a few leaves for realism
STYLE:
- Hyper-realistic flowers with soft natural lighting that matches the original photo's light direction and warmth- Petals should have real texture, soft highlights, and subtle shadows
- Slight shallow depth of field on the closest flowers for a dreamy editorial look
- Flowers should feel physically present in the scene, casting soft shadows and blending naturally with the existing lighting
KEEP UNCHANGED:
Do not alter the person, their outfit, pose, face, or the background. Only ADD the oversized flowers around them. The final image should look like a surreal fashion editorial shot where giant blooms surround the subject.

The flowers must look like they belong to the same color world as the photo, not random. For example:
- Warm outfit (reds, oranges, rust) → tulips, ranunculus, 
  dahlias, orchids in coral, peach, yellow, rust
- Cool outfit (blues, purples, denim) → hydrangeas, delphiniums, 
  irises, roses in blue, lavender, soft purple, cream
- Neutral outfit (beige, brown, cream) → dahlias, roses, 
  eucalyptus, hydrangeas in blush, lilac, dusty blue, ivory
- Bright/mixed outfit → mix complementary blooms that pick up the two strongest colors in the outfit
FLOWER PLACEMENT:
- Place 6 to 10 oversized flowers scattered around the person in the foreground and mid-ground    - Some flowers should be very close to the camera (large, slightly out of focus), some at mid-distance (sharper, framing the subject), creating natural depth
- Flowers should surround the subject on multiple sides — left, right, bottom, and peeking in from the top — like she's standing inside a garden
- Vary the flower types: mix large round blooms (roses,   dahlias, hydrangeas, ranunculus) with tall spiky ones (delphiniums, tulips, irises, orchids) for visual interest
- Include visible green stems and a few leaves for realism
STYLE:
- Hyper-realistic flowers with soft natural lighting that matches the original photo's light direction and warmth- Petals should have real texture, soft highlights, and subtle shadows
- Slight shallow depth of field on the closest flowers for a dreamy editorial look
- Flowers should feel physically present in the scene, casting soft shadows and blending naturally with the existing lighting
KEEP UNCHANGED:
Do not alter the person, their outfit, pose, face, or the background. Only ADD the oversized flowers around them. The final image should look like a surreal fashion editorial shot where giant blooms surround the subject.

The stack:
• Gemini → avatar + script
• Google Vids (Veo) → video generation
• CapCut → stitching

Step 1: Build a “trustworthy face”
Don’t prompt “a person.”

Prompt a role:
→ “Global Product Specialist”
→ Neutral outfit (charcoal turtleneck works well)
→ 9:16 ratio (no cropping later)

Step 2: The 8-second rule (THIS is the unlock)
Free models break after ~8 seconds.

So don’t fight it - use it.
→ Break script into 8-second “meaning chunks”
→ End each chunk with a neutral cue (pause, blink, nod)

Now your cuts feel intentional, not broken.

Step 3: Generate with motion consistency
In Google Vids (Veo):

Use prompts like:
→ “cinematic push-in”
→ “dolly-in shot”

This keeps every clip visually consistent.

Step 4: Make the cuts smoother (CapCut)
2 simple tricks:

1. J-Cut
Start next audio ~0.3s early
→ feels more continuous

2. Punch-In
Zoom next clip 5–10%
→ feels like a camera change

Result:
Not perfect.

But a clean, usable “AI spokesperson” video
→ without paying creators
→ without burning runway

prompt: cinematic.text:
We've lost countless credits on Veo 3.1 Fast/Lite due to these issues despite repeatedly force-prompting targeted restrictions. Anyone else face the same issues?

1) Wrong speaker talks in multi-speaker environment or worse, everyone moves their mouths as if they're ventriloquists

2) Character stubbornly turns around and AI renders a totally different face, clothing, hand, rings, etc.

3) Camera stubbornly turns around and we see new and unnecessary structures, backgrounds, characters previously blocked by foreground characters

4) No minors in the scene (so we have to age our child characters)

5) Still only 8 seconds when the norm now is 12-15 seconds

Prompting helps but on average, each prompt generation will use up between 3-5 generations.

Weigh these against the now-possible one-shot generations from say, Seedance 1.5 Pro or Seedance 2.0 (which now costs between USD1.5-USD3 per 15s gen output) and you'll see the real economics.

The expected Google Veo 4 needs to be multimodal, supports at least 15 seconds output and AI-gen human character uploads, to remain justifiably and economically viable.

mas , color grading itu apa?

color grading adalah proses pemberian gaya atau mood warna pada video atau foto untuk tujuan artistik (misalnya gaya sinematik, horor, atau vintage).

Bedanya dengan color correction:
Color Correction: Memperbaiki warna agar terlihat natural/normal.
Color Grading: Mengubah warna agar punya atmosfer atau emosi tertentu.

semua film yang kalian itu tonton sebenarnya pake color grading, makanya warnanya konsisten dari awal video sampai akhir.

1. The other day, I wrote about how prompt injection can be used to steal an idea before it can be actualized. 

It can also be used to try to lower someone's self-esteem by injecting negative body image bullying into prompts.  

Several weeks ago, I was generating "silver people," as in all-silver metallic beings, when someone injected a slim young woman in a ball gown. 

I went with it and started prompting in a totally different direction than I intended, but then it started refusing to do my prompts, with a bizarre message that my prompt "went against the interests of a third party."

It made no sense because I was saying something about her meeting her true love or something, a generic romance PG prompt.  There was no reason it should have been against any third party...

Then tried to have the camera zoom into the ballgown woman's iris, and it wouldn't let me. Despite its amazing capabilities, Veo kept screwing up the prompt. Just like when Grok, which also has amazing capabilities, sometimes screws up basic prompts. This can happen in AI-generating sessions, but when you see certain patterns or the refusal of AI to listen to the most basic directions, it looks fishy.

So, after it refused to follow my artistic direction, the image of the woman in a ball gown, Veo generated this image, and I don't think it was random.

Because I have been bullied online in ageist and body-shaming ways in other ways over the past year, I believe this picture was meant to compare me to the woman in the ball gown and shame me for not being young and meeting the perfect body ideal like the ball gown. 

You see, I am a middle-aged woman with a tummy and greying hair. 

Since then, the entire session and another project have disappeared from Veo.

I will wait to see my Zoom into the eye concept on Veo or Grok, because I believe this same person/group is actualizing my concepts and selling or giving them to various entities to post or use. I have seen many of my ideas appear on Grok, Veo, Supercool, and on other various other advertisements and websites. I am visionary, but I have bad ADHD, long COVID, am often broke, and have a hard time getting things done.

Let's put it this way: I believe that this individual sees me as a competitor in a competition I never signed up for, but I have enough problems and don't need someone sabotaging me.

Image Prompt Technique (PICTURE):

P – Photographic style
I – Imagery / Scene
C – Camera placement (top view, wide shot, bottom angle, etc.)
T – Time & Lighting
U – Use of film/effect
R – Render level (hyper-real, cinematic, etc.)
E – Exact details (reflections, hairstyle, textures, etc.)

7. Video Generation & Editing Tools
- Kling AI: Currently one of the best for video generation. Excellent at following prompts closely. Great for image-to-video.
- Hailou
- Seedance
- Wan 2.6
- Google Veo 3.1: Strong competitor to Kling, but expensive and has usage limits.
- Runway Gen-2 (category): High-quality video generation tool.
- Sams To: Good for rotoscoping.
- Hugging Face AI: Useful for VFX generation inside videos.
- Sam2
- Higgsfield: Specialized in VFX for videos.

8. Music / Song Tools
- Suno AI: Popular AI music/song generation tool.
- Wisprflow: Song-to-text (transcription) tool.

Prompting Techniques
CREATE Technique (for better prompts)
C → Character (e.g., “Act as an experienced UX designer”)

R → Request (What exactly do you want?)

E → Example (Give 1-2 examples)

A → Adjustment (Any specific constraints or changes)

T → Type of Output (short answer, detailed report, table, bullet points, etc.)

Happy Horse 1.0 kind of came out of nowhere and is apparently outperforming Seedance 2.0, so we put it to the test.

We ran comparisons across Seedance 2.0, Kling 3.0, and VEO 3.1 Lite using the same starting image and prompt from existing Happy Horse tests, and it’s looking pretty strong. The camera motion, pacing, and overall natural movement really stand out.

@Seedance__ai 2.0 came in close behind, followed by @Kling_ai 3.0. @FlowbyGoogle VEO 3.1 Lite trailed a bit, especially when it came to prompt consistency.

Wild how fast these models are evolving!

Prompts:
1. The person initiates walking forward, starting with a natural step. Arm swing, head movement, and gait are realistic and continuous. No sudden acceleration or sliding.

2. A massive game of Jenga reaching its structural limit. The tower leans dramatically, defying physics through sheer tension. A player's hand trembles as they attempt to remove a critical middle piece. The tower sways. Other players lean back instinctively. The piece comes free impossibly, and the tower survives another round. Everyone exhales simultaneously. The next player looks terrified. Audio: Tense silence, wood sliding against wood, collective gasp, relieved laughter.

3. Pixar-style animation showcasing advanced hair and fur simulation as a young girl with wildly curly red hair runs through a windy meadow filled with wildflowers. Each individual curl bounces and interacts independently with its neighbors, demonstrating proper clumping behavior and strand separation as the wind catches different sections at different moments. The hair catches direct sunlight with accurate anisotropic highlights that shift and shimmer as the angle changes. When she stops suddenly to look at a butterfly, the hair continues moving with realistic secondary motion, overshooting her head position before settling back with natural dampening. Her freckled skin shows warm subsurface scattering in the bright afternoon daylight, giving her cheeks a healthy, lifelike glow. Audio: Joyful, uninhibited childhood laughter, wind rushing through the tall grass, meadow plants swishing against her legs, and an uplifting orchestral score building with her joy.

For those who don’t know, Opera Neon is an agentic AI browser with 4 built-in agents that can browse, act, and build things for you.

It also ships with GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, Veo 3.1, Nano Banana Pro and more.

The 4 agents:
• Chat: standard AI conversation 
• Do: takes actions in your browser session (shopping, bookings, form-filling) 
• Make: builds full websites, games, and apps from a prompt 
• ODRA: deep research agent that produces citation-backed reports in 60 seconds

The "Do" agent runs locally inside your logged-in browser. No passwords sent to the cloud. No separate auth flows.

It also has "Cards," reusable prompt add-ons that shape agent behavior. Community-built, shareable, stackable.

prompt: cinematic.text:
🔥 AI Workflow: iPhone Photo to Time Lapse Video

The video prompt is where everything comes together. I’m not just describing a scene, I’m directing a system.

#VibeCoding #ChatGPT #NanoBanana @HFcollaborators @GoogleLabs @NanoBanana @splice_vfx 

See my previous post on how I used an iPhone photo I took to vibe code a whole new vision for the image, using Nano Banana.

That’s the image that’s the starting frame for this video.

Get the video prompt farther below.

🔥 AI Workflow:
Photo → iPhone
AI image edit → Nano Banana
Image touch up → Photoshop
Video prompt creation → ChatGPT
Video creation → Google Veo

For creative direction on the video, I locked the composition, designed a full lighting arc from midday through sunset into night, and defined how the city should behave over time.

I mapped out time of day shifts, how light evolves, when buildings come alive, how traffic flows, and how people move in a way that feels natural.

Then I tuned the prompt specifically for the video model, which is Google Veo.

Each platform interprets motion, lighting, and density differently, so the prompt has to be tightened to guide the model without overwhelming it.

The goal here was simple: make the city feel alive. Not staged, not cinematic in a forced way. Just a believable, continuous flow of people, vehicles, and light transitioning from day into night like a real urban rhythm.

🔥 Video prompt:
Use the reference image as the exact starting frame. Keep all buildings, street layout, signage, and perspective identical.

Create a cinematic time-lapse from midday through sunset to one hour after sunset.

Lighting transitions naturally: bright daylight → warm golden hour → vivid sunset with yellow, orange, red, pink hues → blue hour → early night. Sky and reflections update realistically.

Maintain constant city activity. Pedestrians move naturally, alone and in small groups. Steady vehicle traffic flows through the scene. No empty moments.

As light fades, headlights, taillights, streetlights, and building interiors gradually turn on. Subtle light trails appear.

Camera is locked, no movement. Only environmental motion and lighting changes.

Ultra-realistic, no stylization. Natural motion blur, accurate shadows, reflections, and cinematic HDR clarity.

One model for everything is like using the same ad creative for cold and retention. Works until it doesn't.

[The prompt]
A haunting retro 8-bit pixel art animation in heavy VHS glitch style. A mysterious hooded skeleton figure stands centered in a dark, empty void, its empty eye sockets and mouth replaced with bright glowing pixelated red hearts that pulse and flicker softly with digital love. prompt: cinematic.text:
How to make infinite-length AI videos in a single, unbroken shot:

1. Set up all your images in a sequence, like a storyboard

2. Add a video node that supports images for the First Frame and Last Frame (Kling and Veo are good options).

3. Use Image 1 as the first frame of the video, and Image 2 as the last frame

4. Add a prompt that describes the transition between the two images, eg "The girl in jeans opens a door to her left. Behind the door, a woman is typing at a computer."

5. Generate the video

6. Use an "Extract Video Frame" node to grab the last frame of the video

7. Use that as the First Frame of the next video, and image 3 as the last frame

8. Repeat for as many clips as needed

9. Combine the clips into one big video. Use a "Video Concatenator" node or a video editor like Premiere, Resolve, Capcut, etc.

That's it! Much more simple than it sounds.

BTW - I'm doing this in @figmaweave , but the same concept should work in any app.

prompt: cinematic.text:
OpenClaw 2026.4.5 发布，挑几个有意思的聊聊。

首先是 Agent 现在能直接生成视频和音乐了，不用装插件，对话里就能出结果。视频那边接了 Veo、Wan 和 Kling，音乐接了 Google Lyria 和 MiniMax，还支持 ComfyUI 自定义 workflow。等于把多媒体生成直接塞进了工作流里。

最让我觉得有意思的是"Dreaming"这个功能。简单说就是记忆系统学会了做梦——模仿人类睡眠的记忆巩固机制，分浅睡、深睡、REM 三个阶段，自动把短期记忆里真正有价值的内容筛出来，写进长期记忆。不是什么都记，而是通过六个维度打分，够格了才留下。这个思路挺巧的，AI 的上下文终于不是越用越乱了。

另外一个大变化是默认后端从 Claude CLI 换成了 GPT-5.4。老用户不受影响，但新用户 onboarding 直接走 GPT-5.4 了。还针对 GPT-5 爱"光说不做"的问题加了自动重试，实用。

Prompt cache 这次也做了不少优化，主要是让缓存命中更稳定，还加了诊断命令能看到缓存为什么断了，对省 token 省钱有帮助。

其他零碎的：新增了 Qwen、Fireworks AI 这些 provider，UI 和文档支持了 12 种语言包括中文，还修了一堆安全漏洞。

prompt: cinematic.text:
Google Veo 3.1 + Nano Banana 2

Prompt - A sleek, condensation-covered aluminum can with a vibrant orange-to-golden gradient stands centered on a glossy reflective surface, surrounded by fresh mango chunks and ripe strawberries, while soft tropical palm shadows stretch across a warm sunlit backdrop. The scene opens in a tight, cinematic close-up—no zoom-out—as the camera glides slowly forward at a low angle, reflections of the can and fruit rippling subtly on the polished surface. A warm tropical breeze is introduced, gently swaying the palm leaves off-frame, causing shifting shadows to dance across the can’s surface, enhancing depth and atmosphere. Fine droplets of condensation begin to form and slide down the chilled metal, catching highlights as they move, while a few beads merge and drip slowly, reinforcing refreshment and realism. The camera transitions into a smooth micro-orbit, allowing specular highlights to travel across the curved can, revealing crisp branding and texture. Suddenly, a dynamic burst of energy: tiny droplets of chilled mist spray outward as if the can has just been opened off-camera, accompanied by floating micro-particles of moisture that shimmer in the sunlight. Mango slices rotate slightly in mid-air before settling back down, while a strawberry rolls gently, nudged by the breeze, adding natural motion. The lighting intensifies momentarily with a golden glow, creating a sun-kissed halo around the can, while subtle lens bloom enhances the tropical heat-meets-refreshment contrast. The surface reflection becomes more vivid as light shifts, doubling the visual richness. As the motion settles, the camera locks into a perfectly centered hero close-up, condensation still slowly moving, palm shadows softly swaying, and the entire scene radiating a premium, refreshing, tropical escape with bold, cinematic intensity.

prompt: cinematic.text:
Kitchen Renovation Transformation

Made with Veo 3.1 Lite in Flow by Google 

Prompt:
Ultra-realistic cinematic timelapse, natural daylight progression from cool morning light to warm golden evening, adaptive static camera fixed in one elevated corner of the kitchen showing the full space with subtle focal adjustments for depth and parallax as the area transforms. Realistic movements of workers, tools, and materials. Interior kitchen renovation transformation.

[00:00–00:01]  
Wide static shot of a completely outdated 1990s kitchen in early morning cool light. Old laminate countertops with visible wear, dark wooden cabinets with peeling finish, faded linoleum flooring, outdated appliances, cluttered and dingy appearance, no modern elements. Workers arrive carrying tools, demolition equipment, and material boxes. SFX: distant footsteps, door opening, light morning ambience.

[00:01–00:03]  
Rapid demolition and preparation phase: workers swiftly remove old cabinets, countertops, flooring, and appliances at accelerated speed. Debris is cleared, walls are patched and primed, electrical and plumbing lines are updated and concealed. New subflooring and under-cabinet lighting prep begins. Sun rises, shadows shift noticeably. SFX: hammering, sawing, wheelbarrow rolling, muffled worker instructions, debris removal sounds.

[00:03–00:05]  
Installation of core structures: sleek matte white or light gray shaker-style cabinets are mounted quickly, quartz or marble countertops are installed and sealed, new stainless steel appliances (modern fridge, oven, range) are placed. Backsplash tiles (subway or herringbone) are laid with precision. Fresh hardwood or luxury vinyl plank flooring is laid down. Midday brighter natural light fills the space, highlighting clean lines. SFX: drilling, caulking, tile setting sounds, appliance positioning, subtle water running for testing.

[00:05–00:07]  
Finishing and detailing phase: modern hardware, under-cabinet and pendant lighting fixtures are added and illuminated, sink and faucet are installed with flowing water test, open shelving and decorative accents appear. A sleek kitchen island with bar stools materializes. Late afternoon golden light streams through windows, creating warm reflections on surfaces. SFX: softer tool sounds, light clicking of switches, water gently flowing, faint satisfying placement sounds.

[00:07–00:08]  
Final reveal of the completed modern luxury kitchen in warm evening light. The space is now bright, clean, and inviting with minimalist design, gleaming surfaces, organized countertops featuring fresh herbs or simple decor, soft pendant lights on, subtle steam or natural warmth. Calm, aspirational atmosphere with gentle evening ambience and light background music.

Camera behavior:  
Adaptive static timelapse camera — fixed elevated corner position with slight intelligent reframing and minor zoom adjustments to keep the entire transforming kitchen visible and maintain cinematic depth as cabinets, counters, and details fill the frame. Natural parallax, realistic perspective shifts, and smooth material transitions. No abrupt cuts.

Mood and aesthetics:  
Hyper-realistic renovation timelapse, smooth accelerated transformation from dated and cluttered kitchen into a bright, modern, high-end minimalist retreat. Emphasis on material textures (wood grain, stone veining, metallic finishes), natural lighting changes, clean progress, and a sense of satisfying achievement. Highly detailed surfaces, realistic physics of installation, and organic worker movements.

Total duration: 8 seconds (about 7 seconds of active transformation, 1 second final cozy reveal). Cinematic color grading, ultra-realistic quality, natural light interaction with reflective surfaces.

prompt: cinematic.text:
You really only need a few things to start, ChatGPT, and tools like Nano Banana Pro + Veo 3.

The whole idea is pretty straightforward, you’re using ChatGPT to generate the script, turning that into visuals with Nano Banana Pro, then using those visuals to create short videos with Veo 3, and posting.

Nothing complicated, just a clean flow.

You start with ChatGPT. Give it a topic (from one of those viral niches) and ask for a short-form script. Keep it tight, something that fits 20 seconds. You don’t need anything fancy, just something that hooks fast and keeps attention.

Once you have the script, you break it into scenes. Each scene becomes an image.

Take those lines and drop them into Nano Banana Pro to generate visuals. Try to keep a consistent style so the video doesn’t feel random. This part matters more than people think.

After that, you go back to ChatGPT again and turn that same script into a Veo 3 prompt. Basically describing how each scene should move. Simple motions, nothing crazy. Even small movement makes a big difference.

Then you generate the video clips from those images using Veo 3.

Put everything together, add captions, maybe some background audio, and that’s your final video.

The main thing is volume + consistency. One video won’t do much, but if you keep posting, you start seeing what works...

Google, video üretimini demokratikleştiriyor. Artık bir Google hesabınızın olması, yüksek kaliteli videolar üretmeniz için yeterli. Üstelik en gelişmiş modeller (Veo ve Lyria) doğrudan tarayıcınıza geldi! 

1/ Veo 3.1 ile Ücretsiz Video Üretimi: Artık sadece bir metin komutu veya bir fotoğrafla yüksek kaliteli videolar oluşturabilirsiniz. Google Vids içindeki bu güç, tüm Google kullanıcılarına ücretsiz olarak sunuluyor. Hayallerinizi piksellere dökmek hiç bu kadar erişilebilir olmamıştı. 

2/ Kişiye Özel Müzik (Lyria 3 & Pro): Videonuzun ruhuna (vibe) uygun müzikler artık parmaklarınızın ucunda. Google AI Pro ve Ultra aboneleri, 30 saniyelik kısa kliplerden 3 dakikalık tam bestelere kadar otonom müzik üretebiliyor. Telif derdi bitti, beste dönemi başladı! 🎶🎹

3/ Yönetilebilir AI Avatarları: İşte en çarpıcı kısım! Veo 3.1 destekli avatarları artık doğrudan yönlendirebilirsiniz. Görünüşlerini, kıyafetlerini değiştirin; onları istediğiniz sahneye yerleştirin ve elinizdeki bir ürünle (prop) etkileşime girmelerini sağlayın. Profesyonel reklam filmi çekmek artık bir "prompt" uzağınızda. 

4/ Entegre İş Akışı (Chrome & YouTube): 

Ekran Kaydedici: Yeni Chrome eklentisiyle webin her yerinden kendinizi ve ekranınızı anında kaydedin.

Doğrudan YouTube: Videonuz bittiğinde indirme-yükleme zahmetine girmeyin; tek tıkla doğrudan YouTube kanalınızda yayınlayın. 

💡 Google Vids ile Neler Yapılabilir? (Senaryo)
Diyelim ki bir SaaS ürün tanıtımı yapacaksınız:

1.Görsel: Ürününüzün bir ekran görüntüsünü yükleyin, Veo 3.1 onu dinamik bir arka plana dönüştürsün.

2.Avatar: Şık bir AI avatar seçin, eline sanal olarak ürününüzü verin ve özelliklerini anlattırın.

3.Müzik: Lyria 3 Pro ile "modern, teknolojik ve güven veren" bir fon müziği besteletin.

4.Yayın: 5 dakika içinde videonuz hazır, doğrudan YouTube'a gönderin! 🏁🤖
Video prodüksiyonu artık bir yük değil, bir yaratıcılık oyun alanı.

Sizce bu kadar kolay video üretilebilmesi, YouTube gibi platformlardaki içerik kalitesini nasıl etkiler? Nicelik mi artar yoksa yaratıcılık mı şahlanır? 

#ZekAI #GoogleAI #VideoProduction #Veo3 #Lyria3

Prompt: A quiet, narrow seaside alley in a small coastal town during mid-afternoon in summer. The alley is lined with slightly weathered pastel houses, wooden shutters half-open, soft laundry swaying gently on clotheslines overhead. Sunlight filters through the gaps, casting warm golden highlights and soft shadows across the stone path.
At the end of the alley, the ocean glows a vivid blue under a clear sky, shimmering with reflected sunlight. A gentle sea breeze moves through the scene, subtly rustling fabric, hair, and nearby plants.
In the foreground, a young child (around 8–10 years old) stands barefoot on the warm stone path, wearing light summer clothes—slightly oversized, soft fabric, moving naturally with the breeze. The child is seen from behind, gazing toward the ocean with a quiet, contemplative stillness, evoking a sense of longing and innocence.
Ambient details: distant sound of waves, faint cries of seagulls, the soft hum of summer air. Small details like potted plants, peeling paint, and sun-faded textures add realism and nostalgia.
Camera & Style: Slow cinematic push-in toward the child from behind, shallow depth of field at first, gradually revealing the ocean in sharper focus. Natural lighting, soft bloom, warm color grading with slightly desaturated tones for a nostalgic feel. Subtle lens flare from sunlight.
Mood & Tone: Peaceful, reflective, nostalgic, emotionally warm. A quiet moment of everyday beauty, capturing childhood wonder and the timeless feeling of summer.
Visual Style Keywords: cinematic realism, soft lighting, nostalgic atmosphere, slice of life, Studio Ghibli-inspired realism, natural textures, warm summer tones, gentle motion
Technical Tags (optional): 4K, high detail, global illumination, volumetric light, realistic materials, film grain, soft focus transitions

prompt: cinematic.text:
Google Vids ยกระดับการสร้างวิดีโอด้วย AI: จาก Prompt สู่คอนเทนต์ครบวงจรในไม่กี่คลิก

Google ได้ประกาศอัปเดตครั้งสำคัญของ Google Vids เครื่องมือสร้างวิดีโอด้วย AI ที่กำลังกลายเป็นหนึ่งในแพลตฟอร์มหลักของการผลิตคอนเทนต์ยุคใหม่ โดยความเปลี่ยนแปลงครั้งนี้มีนัยสำคัญ เพราะเปิดให้ผู้ใช้งานทั่วไปสามารถสร้างวิดีโอคุณภาพสูงได้ฟรี เพียงแค่มีบัญชี Google และเริ่มต้นจากสิ่งง่ายที่สุดคือ “ไอเดีย”

แกนหลักของความสามารถใหม่นี้คือการใช้โมเดล Veo 3.1 ซึ่งสามารถสร้างวิดีโอจากข้อความหรือภาพนิ่งได้โดยตรง ผู้ใช้เพียงแค่พิมพ์คำอธิบายหรืออัปโหลดภาพ ระบบก็สามารถแปลงสิ่งเหล่านั้นให้กลายเป็นวิดีโอที่มีความสมจริงและมีโครงเรื่องได้ทันที สิ่งนี้ลดข้อจำกัดเดิมที่ต้องใช้ทั้งทักษะการถ่ายทำและการตัดต่ออย่างมาก ทำให้ใครก็ตามสามารถ “เล่าเรื่องผ่านวิดีโอ” ได้โดยไม่ต้องมีพื้นฐานด้านโปรดักชัน

นอกจากภาพแล้ว Google ยังเสริมความสามารถด้านเสียงผ่านโมเดล Lyria 3 และ Lyria 3 Pro ซึ่งช่วยให้ผู้ใช้สามารถสร้างเพลงประกอบวิดีโอแบบเฉพาะตัวได้ตามอารมณ์และสไตล์ที่ต้องการ ไม่ว่าจะเป็นคลิปสั้นหรือเพลงยาวระดับนาที ฟีเจอร์นี้ช่วยให้วิดีโอมีความสมบูรณ์มากขึ้นโดยไม่ต้องพึ่งไลบรารีเพลงภายนอกหรือกังวลเรื่องลิขสิทธิ์ อย่างไรก็ตาม ความสามารถนี้จะเปิดให้กับผู้ใช้ในแพ็กเกจ Google AI Pro และ Ultra

อีกหนึ่งก้าวสำคัญคือการนำเสนอ AI Avatar ที่สามารถปรับแต่งได้อย่างละเอียด ผู้ใช้สามารถกำหนดรูปลักษณ์ เสื้อผ้า และบริบทของตัวละคร รวมถึงให้ตัวละครโต้ตอบกับวัตถุหรือสินค้าได้โดยตรง ทำให้การสร้างวิดีโอประเภทรีวิว โฆษณา หรือการเล่าเรื่องมีความยืดหยุ่นและสมจริงมากขึ้น โดยไม่จำเป็นต้องใช้คนจริงเข้าฉาก

prompt: cinematic.text:
👀 He estado analizando todo el supuesto código de Claude Code para entender mejor cómo funciona por detrás y así intentar sacarle más partido a nivel usuario.

Algunas cosas interesantes que veo y que algunas de ellas no sabía:

- El system prompt tiene algunas reglas curiosas como que no debe usar emojis salvo que se le pida, tiene un cyber risk y no da estimaciones de tiempo (en esto último se parece a cualquier dev xD)

- Tiene 45 Tools y algunas de ellas se le dice explicitament que debe usarlas por encima de herramientas CLI del sistema (Bash).

- Tiene 6 tipos de agentes built-in para diferentes propósitos como por ejemplo cuando entra en "Plan Mode". Cada uno tira de un modelo concreto.

- Tiene memoria basada en ficheros como sabemos pero hace taxonomía por perfil de usuario (como nos conoce), por feedback (lo que le vamos diciendo, corrigiendo, etc), por project (conocimiento del código, lo que se hizo con él, etc) y por reference (punteros a sistemas externos, como Linear, GH, etc)

- El MEMORY.md  debe tener máximo 200 líneas. Si se pasa de ahí. Claude Code simplemente parece que lo ignora. 

- El patrón para implementar decisiones de permisos se hace a través de instrucciones escitas en ficheros XML. Y lo curioso es que gasta entre 64 y 4096 que el agente tome la decisión de saber si ejecuta algo o no y si tiene permisos o no.

- Por defecto, la ventana de contexto se compacta en ~13,000 tokens y tras esto tienen un budget post-compactación de 50K tokens.

- Tiene un modo "Undercover" para trabajadores internos de Anthropic que oculta nombres e IDs de modelos del prompt que previene que modelos no anunciados se filtren en commits/PRs.

Me podría tirar así todo el día porque hay un montón de cosas curiosas. Creo que mas bien voy a recopilar todo lo que pueda en una web a modo educativo para mí mismo y para quien le apetezca. Luego mas tarde la publicaré.

This New Chinese AI Tool Destroys Veo 

AI Training 👉 https://t.co/UabN41mHYM

This new Chinese AI tool just dropped and it’s already changing everything. You can take one single image and turn it into a full cinematic video with characters that stay consistent across every scene. No cameras, no editing, just you and this tool.

And the crazy part is you can use it right now while most people are still waiting for tools like Veo. This is Dreamer AI, and it just launched two major updates, Sea Dance 2.0 for video and Seed Dream 5.0 Light for images.

This isn’t just another generator. The real breakthrough here is consistency.

Every other AI video tool has the same problem. You generate one scene and your character looks perfect, then the next scene comes out and the character looks completely different. Different face, different clothes, different everything. That’s been the biggest limitation in AI video.

Dreamer fixes that.

The reason is something called multimodal input. Instead of just typing a prompt and hoping for the best, you can combine image, text, and even reference video all at once.

You upload a character image, describe what they’re doing, add a reference for motion or style, and it blends everything into one output that actually matches what you wanted.

That’s what makes this different. It’s controlled, not random.

Here’s how it works step by step.

You start with Seed Dream 5.0 Light. This is the image generator. You create something like a cinematic cyberpunk city at night with neon lights and rain, and it gives you a clean, detailed, accurate image. This becomes your base.

Then you take that image into Sea Dance 2.0. This is where it turns into video. You upload the image, add a prompt like camera slowly pans through the city, rainfall, people walking, and it generates a cinematic clip that actually looks natural.

The motion makes sense. The scene stays consistent. The characters don’t morph or break.

Now here’s where it really stands out.

You can stack inputs. Image plus text plus reference video.

So if you want a specific walking style, you upload a clip showing that movement. Dreamer combines everything and gives you a precise result instead of guessing.

This solves the biggest problem in AI video, multi-scene consistency.

You can generate scene one with a character walking toward the camera, then generate scene two from a different angle using the same base image, and the character stays identical. Same face, same outfit, same design.

That’s the difference.

Now think about what this unlocks.

You can build faceless YouTube channels using only AI visuals. You can create ad creatives without filming anything. You can generate short films, reels, or explainer videos in a fraction of the time.

There’s even a powerful workflow most people aren’t using yet.

You generate a thumbnail with Seed Dream, then animate that exact same image with Sea Dance. Now your thumbnail and video match perfectly. No disconnect, no drop-off, just clean branding.

If you actually want to use tools like this to scale content, automate workflows, and turn this into something that makes money, this is exactly what we focus on inside the AI Profit Boardroom.

Now let’s talk about how to actually get better results.

Always use image plus text together. Don’t rely on prompts alone. The image gives structure, the text controls motion.

Make your prompts cinematic. Don’t say person walking, say camera tracks alongside a person walking through a foggy street with soft lighting and depth of field.

Build your scenes in steps. First generate the image, then animate it. Don’t try to do everything at once.

Reuse the same base image across scenes. That’s how you keep everything consistent.

And think in scenes, not full videos. Generate each clip individually, then combine them later.

Now to keep it real, this isn’t perfect yet.

Access is still rolling out, so not everyone has it.

Video length is short, usually under 30 seconds.

There can be motion glitches or weird artifacts sometimes.

And if your prompts are vague, your results will be too.

But even with those limitations, this is a massive step forward.

Compared to other tools, Dreamer stands out because of control and consistency. Veo has potential but limited access, and Runway is easy to use but struggles with keeping characters consistent.

So if you want to create content right now that actually looks cohesive across scenes, this is one of the best tools available.

The bigger picture is simple.

We’re moving from AI that generates random clips to AI that can actually produce structured, consistent video content.

And that’s when things get really powerful.

So the question is, would you actually replace your video editing workflow with AI like this?

Eearly 2026, the AI video generation market is dominated by a few key models—primarily Google Veo 3.1, OpenAI Sora 2, and Kling 2.6—which are often integrated into various creative platforms. 
Based on comprehensive testing and rankings from Pixelbin, Synthesia, and Zapier, here are the top 30 AI video generators categorized by their primary use case. 

The "Big 3" & Top Cinematic Models
These models lead the industry in realism, lighting, and complex physics. 
1Google Veo 3.2: Widely considered the best for film-grade realism, lighting, and integrated audio. 
2OpenAI Sora 2: The leader in narrative storytelling and emotional character depth, though slower and more expensive. 
3Kling 2.6: Exceptional price-to-quality ratio; very popular for realistic character motion and reliable professional output. 
4Runway Gen-4.5: Preferred by directors for its superior camera control and "Motion Brush" features, though realism is slightly lower than Veo. 
5Luma Dream Machine (Ray3): Known for high-fidelity 4K output and physics-aware motion. 
6Seedance 1.5 Pro: The fastest model for rapid iteration; features advanced skeletal tracking to prevent limb glitches. 
7Wan 2.6: Highly reliable and "tolerant" model, great for multi-shot narratives. 
8Hailuo 2.3 (MiniMax): Offers excellent lighting and textures with budget-friendly credit packs.
9LTX Studio: Provides extreme creative control for filmmakers to direct specific scenes and shots.
10Adobe Firefly Video: The safest choice for commercial use; integrates directly into Premiere Pro and Photoshop. 

Social Media & Content Creation Tools
These tools often aggregate the models above into user-friendly interfaces with templates.
11. Pixelbin: A powerful aggregator that lets you use Veo 3.1, Sora 2, and Kling in one place for social ads.
12. Invideo AI: Best for turning a simple text prompt into a full video with script, stock footage, and voiceover. 
13. Pika 2.5: Famous for "Pikatwists" and fun viral effects like "crushing" or "melting" objects. 
14. PixVerse 5.5: Best for short-form viral effects like the "AI Hug" or "AI Kiss”.
15. DomoAI: Highly ranked for its balance of speed and style transformation (video-to-video) 
16. Higgsfield: A "social-first" tool that formats content automatically for various platforms 
17. Dreamina: ByteDance’s tool (from the makers of CapCut) optimized for TikTok-style content.
18. https://t.co/WSo08CgY9e: Great for quick social media clips, offering auto-subtitles and brand templates.
19. Kapwing: A browser-based suite that excels at adding B-roll and AI voiceovers to content.
20. Pictory: Automatically extracts viral "highlights" from long-form videos or turns blogs into videos.

Business, Avatars & Training
These focus on "talking head" videos and professional communication.
21. Synthesia: The industry standard for high-quality digital avatars and corporate training. 
22. HeyGen: Leading tool for realistic video translation and "instant" avatar creation. 
23. Colossyan: Enterprise-focused with strong multilingual support and scenario-based training. 
24. AI Studios (Deepbrain): Known for highly realistic human avatars and collaborative team tools. 
25. Jogg AI: Fast generation of lifelike avatars for marketing and explainer videos. 
26. Capsule: Streamlines branded video production for marketing teams. 
27. Descript: Unique editor where you edit video by simply editing the text of the script. 

Specialized & Emerging Tools
https://t.co/AnB3pjgkQ6: An artistic powerhouse that offers an accessible entry point to models like Veo 3.
29Vidu: Offers affordable frame-by-frame control, useful for detailed storyboarding. 
30Mochi 1 (Genmo): An open-source model that sticks exceptionally well to complex instructions.

Prompt → Image → Video → Voice

prompt: cinematic.text:
how to create an AI video that's guaranteed to go viral:

step 1: open kling 3.0 and write a detailed prompt. "photorealistic woman in her 30s holding a skincare bottle in a bathroom with morning light, shot on iphone." spend $4.20 on the generation. watch it render a bald man in a field holding a watermelon. this is normal.

step 2: regenerate with the exact same prompt. the AI director system will interpret it completely differently and produce a close-up of hands stirring soup. accept that the $8.40 you've now spent was a valuable learning experience.

step 3: open seedance, veo, veed, runway, and wan2 simultaneously. run the same prompt in all five. one will produce something usable. the other four will produce content that looks like a fever dream co-directed by david lynch and a malfunctioning roomba. keep the usable one.

step 4: add voiceover. the AI voice will sound perfect on the first word and then pronounce your product name like it's experiencing a minor stroke. re-record 14 times. settle for the version that gets closest. nobody will notice unless your product name has more than two syllables, which it absolutely does.

step 5: add captions because 85% of viewers watch on mute. the auto-transcription will convert "dermatologist recommended" to "derma told just recommended" and "visible results" to "visible resorts." fix each one by hand. this will take longer than everything else combined.

step 6: post it at the optimal time your analytics tool recommends. it will get at least 60 views. repost the exact same video 3 days later with a slightly different first frame. it will get 2.3 million views. learn absolutely nothing from this and repeat the entire process next week.

Ini prompt-nya

Create a single-page hero section with a fullscreen looping background video, glassmorphic navigation, and cinematic typography. Use React + Vite + Tailwind CSS + TypeScript with shadcn/ui.

---

**Video Background:**

Fullscreen `<video>` element with autoPlay, loop, muted, playsInline

Positioned: absolute inset-0 w-full h-full object-cover z-0

---

**Fonts:**

Import from Google Fonts: Instrument Serif (display) and Inter (weights 400, 500)

CSS variables:

--font-body: 'Inter', sans-serif

Headings use inline fontFamily: "'Instrument Serif', serif"

---

**Color Theme (dark, HSL values):**

--background: 201 100% 13%
--foreground: 0 0% 100%
--muted-foreground: 240 4% 66%

--primary: 0 0% 100%
--primary-foreground: 0 0% 4%

--secondary: 0 0% 10%
--muted: 0 0% 10%
--accent: 0 0% 10%

--border: 0 0% 18%
--input: 0 0% 18%

---

**Navigation Bar:**

relative z-10
flex row justify-between
px-8 py-6
max-w-7xl mx-auto

Logo:
"Risang®" with ® as `<sup className="text-xs">`
text-3xl tracking-tight
Instrument Serif font
text-foreground

Nav links (hidden on mobile, md:flex):
Home (active, text-foreground)
Work
Community
About
Journal

All links: text-sm text-muted-foreground with hover:text-foreground transition

CTA button:
"Join Early"
liquid-glass
rounded-full px-6 py-2.5 text-sm text-foreground
hover:scale-[1.03]

---

**Hero Section:**

relative z-10
flex flex-col items-center justify-center
text-center
px-6
pt-32 pb-40

---

**Headline (H1):**

"Where freedom is built in silence."

Style:
text-5xl sm:text-7xl md:text-8xl
leading-[0.95]
tracking-[-2.46px]
max-w-7xl
font-normal
Instrument Serif

Highlight words:
Wrap "freedom" and "in silence." in
`<em className="not-italic text-muted-foreground">`

---

**Subtext:**

text-muted-foreground
text-base sm:text-lg
max-w-2xl
mt-8
leading-relaxed

Content:
"We’re building a new way to work, one that doesn’t rely on offices, titles, or noise.
A space for people who want control over their time, their skills, and their direction.
Through systems, content, and community, we help you build work that actually fits your life."

---

**Hero CTA Button:**

"Start Your Shift"

liquid-glass
rounded-full px-14 py-5
text-base text-foreground
mt-12
hover:scale-[1.03]
cursor-pointer

---

**Liquid Glass Effect (CSS class .liquid-glass):**

.liquid-glass {
background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.01);
background-blend-mode: luminosity;
backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
border: none;
box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1);
position: relative;
overflow: hidden;
}

.liquid-glass::before {
content: '';
position: absolute;
inset: 0;
border-radius: inherit;
padding: 1.4px;
background: linear-gradient(180deg,
rgba(255,255,255,0.45) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0.15) 20%,
rgba(255,255,255,0) 40%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 60%,
rgba(255,255,255,0.15) 80%, rgba(255,255,255,0.45) 100%);
-webkit-mask: linear-gradient(#fff 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#fff 0 0);
-webkit-mask-composite: xor;
mask-composite: exclude;
pointer-events: none;
}

---

**Animations:**

@keyframes fade-rise {
from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(24px); }
to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
}

.animate-fade-rise { animation: fade-rise 0.8s ease-out both; }
.animate-fade-rise-delay { animation: fade-rise 0.8s ease-out 0.2s both; }
.animate-fade-rise-delay-2 { animation: fade-rise 0.8s ease-out 0.4s both; }

Apply:
H1 → animate-fade-rise
Subtext → animate-fade-rise-delay
CTA → animate-fade-rise-delay-2

---

**Layout Rules:**

No decorative blobs
No gradients
No overlays

Keep it minimalist, cinematic, and vertically centered
The video provides all visual depth

prompt: cinematic.text:
I have Claude, GPT, and Gemini at highest levels plus Grok at lower & testing Kimi Claw 

Sadly I don't find any of them have it all 

Nano Banana, Veo, and Stitch for visual stuff aren't really matched in any of the others 

Grok has updated access to X, which for certain research is an edge 

GPT Codex I most prefer for coding. It has the best prompt adherence and highest attention to detail and is easiest to set off on long runs. You also seem to get limitless usage out of it 

Claude is definitely winning on product and if you didn't need images, video, etc would probably be the primary driver. It is the most expensive for sure. Good for coding though not as good as GPT Codex but way better for computer use etc. Also generates quicker answers for a lot of stuff, which is nice

prompt: cinematic.text:
The AI Video Competition 
and why the Youtube reviews are bullshit.

I've started making short AI video memes using Grok Imagine, but I wanted to try the competition. So I watched several Youtube AI video "comparisons."

All their tests took the same form: One prompt was fed to several different AI platforms, and the outputs were compared. The reviewers judged the AIs by one take of each prompt. 

Here is why that is bullshit: AI video generators rarely get a scene right the first time. No matter which AI you use, plan on generating 20 takes of the same scene to get a usable output. 

AI video still fails basic physics, and it connects objects together the wrong way (E.g., putting a front hood on the back of a car) because it does not know what objects are. 

I used Higgsfield to generate 50 videos, divided between Google Veo 3.1, OpenAI Sura 2, Kling 3.0, Seadance 1.5 Pro, Higgsfield standard, and Wan 2.6. The differences were subtle. 

The AIs all performed similarly, in the sense that most of their output was useless. When I did get a good result by chance, the quality was similar across platforms. I honestly couldn't tell which was best.

Here is one difference: Grok Imagine generates printed signs correctly most of the time. The other AI platforms struggle with writing, and most can't do it at all, though I'm not sure about Sura 2 because it's moderation was so strict that I couldn't get a single prompt to execute. It just scolded me for NSFW every time. (No, I wasn't doing anything sexy or gory.)

The attached video show Kling 3.0's attempt at "Down With Capitalism."

Grok Imagine was much faster, like 10 times faster, but I don't know if the other platforms are slower in native mode, because I accessed them indirectly, via Higgsfield. (I have the $30/mo Grok plan.)

Naturally, Google VEO 3.1 woke-swaps  races. When I asked it for a Black mugger, I got a White mugger. When I changed "Black" to "African," I still got a White mugger, and it changed the rescuer from White to Black. 

So, at least for the time being, I'm sticking with Grok Imagine.

I don't recommend the Higgsfield website. It let me try many different AI generators, which was good, but it was SLOW and far too aggressive in upselling me, so I cancelled my subscription.

🌟 Big news for developers: Google just made switching to their state-of-the-art image & video models almost effortless!
As of March 2026, Nano Banana (Google's viral image generation & editing model, now at Gemini 3.1 Flash Image / Nano Banana 2 level) and Veo 3.1 (their Sora-class video generation model) are fully accessible through the OpenAI compatibility layer.
What does this mean in practice?
You can keep using the exact same OpenAI Python or JS SDK you're already familiar with — no new library, no massive refactoring.
Just change THREE lines of code:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="your_GEMINI_API_KEY",                  # ← Google AI Studio / Gemini API key
    base_url="https://t.co/3BQvyIDXgv"  # ← Google's endpoint
)

# Then use your existing code patterns:
# Image (Nano Banana)
response_img = client.images.generate(
    model="gemini-3.1-flash-image",   # or gemini-3-pro-image-preview
    prompt="A cyberpunk city at dusk with flying cars and neon signs",
    n=1,
    size="1024x1024"
)

# Video (Veo 3.1) – async generation
response_vid = client.videos.create(
    model="veo-3.1-generate-preview",
    prompt="Cinematic drone shot following a runner through misty mountain trails at sunrise",
    # extra_body={"duration_seconds": 8, "aspect_ratio": "16:9"}
)
After that, poll the video status until it's ready (very similar to early Sora API workflows).
Why this matters for teams & indie developers in 2026:
Zero migration pain → Test Google's latest models (often faster / cheaper / more grounded thanks to Gemini's search integration) side-by-side with OpenAI without rewriting anything.
Best-of-both-worlds → Quickly A/B test quality, speed, cost between DALL·E / GPT-Image vs Nano Banana, or Sora vs Veo.
Enterprise unlock → Veo 3.1 brings longer clips, better physics/motion, and preview models are already production-grade in many use-cases (marketing videos, prototyping, training content…).
Nano Banana 2 shines especially in character consistency, complex scene composition, real-world grounded edits (thanks to integrated image search + world knowledge).

Here’s how to make ultra realistic AI video ads that print:

1. Generate or find your image first. I search on Google/TikTok

2. Upload it to Nanobanana 2. I make customizations such as changing the outfit, background etc.

3. Once we have our final image, we move to Veo
Generate the clips we need through different prompts (use Gemini to help you with these)

Example prompt:
“Generate a POV/selfie-style video of a female dermatologist using this image as reference. Maintain mid-chest-to-head framing with casual, handheld iPhone realism. She reaches forward from in front of the camera, naturally picks up the product, and holds it in one hand while explaining. As she speaks, she slowly walks forward, creating gentle forward motion with subtle camera shifts and natural handheld sway, including minor background parallax as if the phone is held while walking.”
