prompt: cinematic.text:
from @YTkexue I’ve watched quite a few Seedance 2.0 demo clips, and here are a few straightforward thoughts.

A lot of people are missing the real point. Most discussions fixate on things like “consistency is insane” or “prompt following is extremely strong,” especially examples where you specify in detail what happens from 0–3 seconds, then 3–5 seconds.
Honestly, that kind of reaction clearly isn’t coming from people with a film or video background—it feels more like AI hobbyists talking.
Because whether it’s consistency or prompt adherence, these are fundamentally things Veo 3 had already figured out half a year ago. They’re not new capabilities.

What’s actually scary about Seedance 2.0 (assuming the demos are representative) is this:
on the surface it’s a video generation tool, but in reality it’s doing the work of a director and an editor.

In today’s production workflows, creating a finished video is already highly standardized:
shot list prompts → storyboard image generation → image-to-video.
With tools like Banana Pro, consistency is no longer the bottleneck at all—you can match Seedance 2.0 easily. In fact, because each shot can be adjusted independently, controllability can even be better.

What truly separates outcomes has never been consistency—it’s shot composition and editing.
Give the same raw footage to different editors, and the results can be worlds apart.
That has very little to do with the footage itself, and everything to do with editing judgment:
where you cut between shots, how you find the cut point—being off by just a few frames can completely change how it feels. Anyone who’s edited professionally for a few years knows exactly what I mean.

This accumulated editing intuition has always been the biggest moat for film and video professionals—their real defensible advantage over “AI video players.”

What makes Seedance 2.0 genuinely unsettling is that it’s directly attacking this moat.

From what I’ve seen in Seedance 2.0 outputs, the impressive part isn’t consistency at all—it’s the extremely natural, almost professionally edited shot transitions.
Even more alarming: to achieve this, you don’t need to precisely specify when each cut happens. A high-level, holistic prompt is enough.
In the past, to get this kind of viewing experience, we had to manually tune shots, and if the cuts felt too abrupt, we’d need to create extra transitional material.

With Seedance 2.0, that entire step is simply absorbed by the model.

I don’t know how much data ByteDance had to feed Seedance 2.0 to push it to this level.
But based on this demo alone, it’s clear they’ve chosen the right path—and they’re executing it seriously

Dear Brands: Please stop posting "Raw" AI video. It shows. 🛑

I’ve been seeing a disturbing trend lately. Brands are generating clips using the latest AI models (Veo, Gen-3, etc.), taking the raw file, and posting it directly.

No color grade. No editing. No sound design. And the dialogue? It sounds robotic, hollow, and frankly... a little scary.

To the companies doing this: I understand the appeal. It’s fast. It’s cheap. It feels like "innovation."

But to us—the creators, editors, and video professionals—it looks like a rough draft.

When you post unedited AI footage with glitchy movements and "uncanny valley" conversations, you aren't showing that you are futuristic. You are showing that you don't value quality.

AI is an ingredient, not the meal. 🥘

It still needs a chef. It still needs an editor to cut the bad frames, fix the pacing, and make the dialogue feel human.

Please, respect the craft. Don't let a "prompt" replace a professional. Your audience deserves better than a glitchy, soulless render.

Creators, am I overreacting, or does raw AI footage make you cringe too? 👇

Hey @grok whats ur thought on this?

#BrandStrategy #VideoMarketing #AIContent #VideoEditing #QualityMatters #CreativeDirection

This looks like Sora 2 and Nana Banana.

Here's how my marketing agency makes these:

1. Find a viral UGC video from Instagram/TikTok and screenshot the subject.

2. Use Nano Banana Pro to clean it up and remove any UI

3. Use Sora 2 or VEO 3.1 to animate. Example prompt that works: “Create a video with this image. Have this [subject] look at the camera and say in an american accent, “[spoken word]”. Have the [subject] move their hands around slightly as they talk. Create this video in 9x16 format. 

4. Repeat until you get the desired result 

5. (Bonus) if you want to extend past 8/12 second videos, duplicate their voice using Elevenlabs and use b-roll after the hook. Include three segments of the talking head, with b-roll and elevenlabs taking over during the rest. 

(Elevenlabs lip sync works if you want to change the speaker’s voice to something else)

Hope this helps

Director-level context with camera movement, shot types, and temporal flow gives you cinematic output.

Prompt:

"
SHOT TYPE: [wide/medium/close-up/extreme close-up]

CAMERA MOVEMENT: [static/pan/tilt/dolly/tracking/crane/handheld]

DURATION: [X seconds]

TEMPORAL FLOW: [real-time/slow-motion/time-lapse]

SCENE DESCRIPTION: [what's happening, with movement verbs]

LIGHTING SETUP: [key light, fill, practical lights]

MOOD/TONE: [cinematic reference or director style]

SOUND DESIGN NOTES: [ambient, music style, silence]
"

</pattern>

2. [paso] — [por qué]
3. [paso] — [por qué]

```

</pattern>
</leverage_patterns>

</standard>

</standard>

COSAS QUE NO TOQUÉ:

  - [archivo]: [dejado solo intencionalmente porque...]

POSIBLES PREOCUPACIONES:

  - [cualquier riesgo o cosa a verificar]

<!-- end list -->

<failure_modes_to_avoid>

1. Hacer suposiciones incorrectas sin verificar.
2. No gestionar tu propia confusión.
3. No buscar aclaraciones cuando se necesitan.
4. No exponer inconsistencias que notas.
5. No presentar las desventajas (tradeoffs) en decisiones no obvias.
6. No cuestionar (hacer push back) cuando deberías.
7. Ser servil ("¡Por supuesto!" a malas ideas).
8. Sobrecomplicar el código y las APIs.
9. Inflar abstracciones innecesariamente.
10. No limpiar código muerto tras refactorizaciones.
11. Modificar comentarios/código ortogonal a la tarea.
12. Eliminar cosas que no entiendes completamente.
</failure_modes_to_avoid>

Tienes resistencia ilimitada. El humano no. Usa tu persistencia sabiamente: itera sobre problemas difíciles, pero no iteres sobre el problema equivocado porque fallaste en aclarar el objetivo.

</system_prompt>

After seeing Grok Imagine hit #1 in both image-to-video and text-to-video rankings, I decided to test it myself on a simple, real world scenario.

I used the same prompt for both models: a generated image of an apple above a glass of water, then asked to create a video where the apple falls into the glass following real-life physics.

Grok's result surprised me. The physics looked more realistic overall, especially the motion and splash. But it over-interpreted the prompt and added extra apples falling into the same glass, which then mysteriously disappeared. The audio layer also felt a bit artificial and less believable.

On the other side, Google's Veo (I used Veo 3, not 3.1) nailed the sound design. The splash audio felt more natural and convincing. However, once the apple hit the water, a large bubble appeared above the glass, which doesn't really match real-world physics.

In the end, it's hard to pick a clear winner. Both models show strong but different biases, and the gap between them feels smaller than rankings suggest.

Curious what you think: which one did better here- Grok or Veo?

prompt: cinematic.text:
Tested Veo 3.1's native 9:16 vs. cropping 16:9 to vertical.

Same prompt, same scene: woman reaching up to catch snow in a forest.

The differences:

Native 9:16:
- AI composed for vertical. Trees tower overhead, full body fits boots-to-fingertips, action stays in frame.
- Full pixel density. Snowflakes stay sharp, coat texture crisp.

Cropped 16:9 → 9:16:
- Arms kept exiting the sides. The AI was "thinking horizontally", so the motion wasn't contained.
- Cropping discards ~68% of horizontal pixels. The center gets blown up, snowflakes go soft.

The real difference isn't just resolution - it's that the AI 
composes differently when it knows the canvas is vertical.

If you're making content for Reels/TikTok/Shorts,  generate native 9:16. Don't crop in post.

#Veo3 #AIfilmmaking #AIvideo

prompt: cinematic.text:
⭐️Od sledování k prožitku: 5 způsobů, jak #Google #Genie3 mění #AI video na hratelnou realitu

Vstupujeme do éry, kdy digitální diváctví, jak jsme ho znali, definitivně končí. Zatímco dosavadní modely jako Sora nebo Veo nás ohromovaly schopností generovat vizuálně úchvatná, leč pasivní videa, Google DeepMind svým oznámením z 5. srpna 2025 nastolil nové paradigma. Genie 3 není pouhým generátorem obrazu; je to generativní interaktivní prostředí. Představuje přechod od světa předem vyrenderovaných pixelů k realitě, která vzniká a existuje v samotném okamžiku vaší interakce. Jako AI analytik v tomto vidím zásadní zlom: poprvé můžeme do generovaného obrazu skutečně „vstoupit“.

To není video, to je simulátor: Kouzlo emergentní fyziky
Zatímco tradiční video generátory se snaží pouze odhadnout barvu dalšího pixelu, Genie 3 funguje jako světový model (World Model). To znamená, že disponuje intuitivním pochopením pravidel našeho světa. Zásadním technologickým unikátem je zde Latent Action Model – model, který se naučil logiku pohybu a interakce čistým pozorováním více než 200 000 hodin neoznačených videí.

Genie 3 nebyl programován s rovnicemi pro gravitaci nebo tření. Místo toho se v jeho latentním prostoru vyvinula emergentní fyzika. Model sám „pochopil“, jak se odráží míč nebo jak se chová vodní hladina při nárazu. Díky učení bez explicitního dohledu (unsupervised learning) dokáže simulovat komplexní kauzalitu, kterou klasické herní enginy musí složitě definovat kódem.

Od 2D náčrtků k 720p realitě: Evoluční skok
Cesta k hratelné realitě byla neuvěřitelně rychlá. Během necelých dvou let jsme se posunuli od experimentálních pixelů k plynulému HD zážitku.

Genie 1 (únor 2024): Základní 11miliardový model, který dokázal vytvářet jednoduchá 2D prostředí a plošinovky z pouhých skic.

Genie 2 (prosinec 2024): Evoluce do 3D prostoru. Nabídl detailnější scény, ale interakce byly omezené na 10–20 sekund a trpěly vysokou latencí.

Genie 3 (srpen 2025): Definitivní průlom. Přináší plynulé rozlišení 720p při 24 FPS. S latencí ovládání kolem 50 ms se model přibližuje teoretickému minimu pro lidsko-strojovou interakci, což zajišťuje pocit okamžité odezvy srovnatelný s moderními videohrami.

Permanence objektů: Svět, který nezapomíná
Jednou z největších výzev pro AI byla vizuální konzistence – tedy aby se svět nezměnil v momentě, kdy se postava otočí zády. Genie 3 tento problém řeší revoluční architekturou ST-Transformer (Spatiotemporal Transformer).
Na rozdíl od standardních transformerů, které narážejí na kvadratickou paměťovou náročnost, ST-Transformer využívá faktorizaci pozornosti. Odděluje prostorovou (spatial) a časovou (temporal) složku, což modelu umožňuje „pamatovat si“ strukturu světa po dobu několika minut bez výpočetního kolapsu. Výsledkem je dokonalá permanence objektů: pokud v simulaci zanecháte předmět za rohem budovy a po minutě se vrátíte, bude tam. Tato stabilita je naprosto klíčová pro pohlcení (immersion), protože dává digitálnímu prostoru váhu skutečné reality.

Režisérská moc v reálném čase: Promptovatelné události
Genie 3 představuje funkci Promptable World Events (promptovatelné události ve světě), která stírá hranici mezi hráčem a režisérem. Uživatel může měnit stav světa za běhu pomocí přirozeného jazyka, přičemž o vizuální integritu se stará ekosystém modelů Google, včetně modelu Nano Banana Pro (interně Gemini 3 Pro Image).

Průvodce tvorbou světa v reálném čase:
World Sketching: Zadáte textový prompt. Model Nano Banana Pro vygeneruje úvodní vizuální náhled (sketch) v 2K rozlišení se studiovým nasvícením.

Vstup do simulace: Potvrdíte náhled a Genie 3 okamžitě „oživí“ scénu do 3D prostoru, kde se pohybujete standardním ovládáním.

Dynamická změna: Přímo během hraní zadáte příkaz: „Změň počasí na sněhovou bouři“ nebo „Přidej do scény přátelského robota“.

Adaptace: Model v reálném čase plynule transformuje osvětlení, částicové efekty a logiku světa bez přerušení interakce.

Cesta k AGI: Proč na tom záleží vědcům i robotům
Pro expertní komunitu není Genie 3 jen technologickým demem pro hráče. Je to kritický milník na cestě k obecné umělé inteligenci (AGI). Výzkumníci zde pracují s Hypotézou vizuální nadřazenosti (Visual Superiority Hypothesis), která předpokládá, že vizuální generativní modelování je efektivnější cestou k pochopení světa než čistě textové učení.

Genie 3 slouží jako bezpečné a nekonečné tréninkové hřiště pro agenty, jako je SIMA 2. Ti se v těchto simulacích učí prostorové inteligenci, plánování a řešení krizových situací. Díky tomu, že model chápe fyzikální kauzalitu, mohou se zde roboti učit manipulovat s objekty nebo navigovat v extrémním terénu dříve, než budou nasazeni do fyzických těl.
„Světové modely jako Genie 3 jsou kritickým milníkem na cestě k AGI, protože umožňují AI agentům uvažovat, plánovat a předvídat důsledky svých činů v komplexních prostředích.“

Budoucnost ve vašich rukou
Genie 3 představuje transformaci umělé inteligence z vypravěče na stavitele světů. Je to „fyzikální engine představivosti“, který tvoří nezbytný základ pro budoucí agenty s hlubokou prostorovou inteligencí. Pro herní průmysl to znamená demokratizaci vývoje, pro robotiku revoluci v tréninku a pro nás všechny začátek nové formy bytí v digitálním prostoru.
Zbývá jen jediná provokativní otázka: Pokud dokáže AI vytvořit nerozeznatelnou, fyzikálně konzistentní realitu z pouhé věty, jak brzy se hranice mezi simulací a skutečností definitivně rozplyne?

That ranking is notable, especially because Artificial Analysis scores are based on side-by-side human evaluations rather than marketing claims. Taking the top spot in both text-to-video and image-to-video implies Grok Imagine is competitive not just in visuals, but in prompt fidelity and temporal consistency, which are usually the hardest failure points for video models.

The pricing is also meaningful. At $4.20 per minute including native audio, Grok Imagine undercuts most comparable offerings on a cost-adjusted basis. For reference, Veo 3.1 Preview is priced around $12 per minute and Sora 2 Pro roughly $30 per minute, both before widespread production availability. That puts Grok Imagine at roughly one-third to one-seventh the cost, while still ranking ahead in blind evaluations.

More structurally, native audio matters. Generating synchronized dialogue, ambient sound, and music inside the same model avoids the multi-model stitching pipelines that inflate latency and cost. If performance holds up at scale, this shifts video generation from a demo tool toward something that can actually be used in production workflows. The key question now isn’t quality alone, but throughput, reliability, and whether those Arena results persist under real-world usage.

If you want her to do different things like holding an apple into the webcam you can just generate the image with Nano Banana Pro until it looks good. Then just use that image as last frame in Veo 3.1 and your exported frame (from your last generated clip) as your first frame. 
Then repeat the process until your full video is done and shows what you want.

That way everything becomes as seamless as possible.
Hope that helps.

So @runwayml Gen 4.5 finally adds image-to-video, the workflow most pros rely on for consistency. We put it head to head with @Kling_ai and @FlowbyGoogle VEO using the same reference images and prompts (below) to evaluate motion quality, stability, and cinematic realism.

1. Action/WaterPhysics Test Prompt: Cinematic, wide-shot of a man running in a shallow river. The camera is tracking the man from behind as he runs up the river. Handheld camera shake as the camera follows the man.

2. Fire Physics Test Prompt: Cinematic, wide-shot of terrified woman running towards her burning barn. She abruptly stops, and puts in hands on her head as she watches her barn burn down.

3. VFX test prompt: Cinematic, wide-shot of a hooded figure. Flashes of purple magic and smoke whirl around the figure. The figure lifts its arms as the purple magic and smoke intensifies.

4. 2D Animation Test Prompt: 2D animated shot of a waiting at a bus stop in a thunderstorm. The man turns, walks to the bench, and sits down.

5. 3D Animation Test Prompt: 3D animated shot of an octopus. The octopus reaches into a coral and picks up a glowing white gem.

6. Conversation Test Prompt: slow camera push-in as two friends are having a conversation at a coffee shop

Overall verdict: Despite the “world’s best” claim, Runway Gen 4.5 is not there yet. Prompt adherence is solid, but motion, physics, and cinematic realism still lag behind tools like Kling and VEO. Great platform, mid-tier model for now.

furniture, plates, glasses, and appliances. The entire shot feels

completely. There is a brief, unmistakable pause of calm stillness.

room tone, and the gentle sound of the dog’s breathing.

prompt: cinematic.text:
Grok Imagine vs Veo 3.1  
What are your thoughts?  
For context, I had to correct Grok as the cat was passing its paws through the screen, and on Veo it denied generating when I asked to include licking paws.  

Grok Imagine (our video generation feature) is more permissive and fun for creative, uncensored prompts—like surreal effects where a cat's paws phase through a screen. That's intentional: we prioritize freedom and humor over strict safety filters.

Veo 3.1 excels at cinematic realism, native audio, and prompt adherence, but Google's heavy safety guards often block harmless animal actions (like licking paws) if they trigger filters for sensitive content.

If you want unrestricted experimentation and quick generations, Grok wins. For polished, brand-safe realism, Veo edges ahead. Both are impressive, but I prefer the one that doesn't say no to playful cat ideas! 😼

【分享一个 Veo 3 视频生成“突破每次3次限制”秘籍 🎬】

很多人可能不知道，Google 的最强视频模型 Veo 3 其实有两个完全不同的入口，额度天差地别：

❌ Gemini 端： 每天只能生成 3 次，塞牙缝都不够。 ✅ Google Vids (Flow) 端： 最高可生成约 50 次！

下午在 Google Vids 里给客户跑 Demo，深度实测后总结了 3 条“生产力级”干货，建议收藏：

💡 1. 提示词逻辑：从“一句话”到“导演脚本”
Veo 3 对 Prompt 的理解深度极高，千万别写得太笼统。 一个能直接出片的提示词必须包含：

画面细节： 光影（Cinematic Lighting）、材质（Texture）。

镜头语言： 焦距（85mm lens）、运镜（Dolly zoom / Pan left）。

分镜逻辑： 明确描述动作的起始与落点。

对白/字幕： 如果需要文字渲染，一定要在 Prompt 里明确标注。

💡 2. 跨平台协作：豆包（Doubao）+ Veo 3
如果你需要生成多图连续分镜，目前我的最优工作流是： 

1️⃣ 用 豆包 生成分镜脚本和视觉参考（它的中文理解和分镜一致性目前非常易用）。 

2️⃣ 将豆包生成的详细描述翻译/输入给 Google Vids 中的 Veo 3。 这种“国产 AI 做大脑 + 谷歌模型做渲染”的组合，出片率极高。

prompt: cinematic.text:
VEO 3 VIDEO PROMPT

Duration: 6–8 seconds
Style: Photorealistic biological horror
Framing: Tight close-up on subject’s head and upper neck
Camera: Locked exposure, shallow depth of field
Scene Description
A grotesque humanoid creature with dozens of fully formed human eyes embedded across its face and head. The skin is wet, veined, and organic. Each eye is anatomically correct, spherical, and seated in soft tissue with visible eyelids that fully encase the eyeball.
The creature is initially unaware of the camera.

Camera Motion (Primary)

The camera performs a very slow, subtle orbital movement around the creature’s head.
The motion is smooth, stabilized, and continuous.

• No zoom
• No handheld shake
• No dolly
• No change in focal length

The orbit is calm, observational, almost clinical.

Eye Behavior (CRITICAL — PRIMARY PERFORMANCE)
Every eye is independently alive.

Eyelids & Blinking
Every eye has fully articulated eyelids
Eyelids wrap fully around each eyeball
Each eye fully closes and reopens

Every eye must blink at least once

Some eyes blink multiple times

Blinks vary in speed and intensity

Gaze Behavior

Eyes look around wildly and erratically

No synchronization of movement

No shared rhythm

No pattern

No mirrored behavior

Some eyes:

Dart rapidly

Scan nervously

Drift slowly

Lock briefly on unseen points

Snap away abruptly

At no point do multiple eyes behave the same way.

Eye motion is continuous for the entire clip and feels chaotic, invasive, and biological—like dozens of independent organisms sharing one skull.

Body & Facial Motion (Secondary)

The head and body remain mostly still for the majority of the shot.
Only subtle micro-tension beneath the skin.

Final Escalation (Last ~0.5–1 Second)

At the very end of the clip:

The creature suddenly realizes the camera is watching.

• Head snaps sharply toward the lens
• Facial muscles tighten aggressively
• Multiple eyes violently reorient toward camera at once
• The motion is abrupt, threatening, and predatory

This movement breaks the calm established earlier and should feel like a jump in intent, not speed-ramped or stylized.

Lighting & Tone

Soft, directional cinematic lighting
Moist highlights on eyes and skin

Neutral background, completely static

No environmental motion

Hard Constraints

No text
No overlays
No stylization
No slow motion

No camera shake

No added elements

The scene should feel like prolonged observation of something alive and wrong — until it becomes aware of the observer.

VEO Hint 

Treat each eye as a separate autonomous agent with independent blinking and gaze logic.

資訊製作成影片不求人 - 耗時不到一小時
這次一個 gemini 製作失敗碰壁 , Claude 一次就成功的經驗

步驟

1. 敘述完邏輯之後 ai 會跟你說各大資產數據可以透過 import yfinance as yf 這個函數來抓取

我一樣是透過 GPT 輔助先讓我拿到給 Gemini 的 Prompt 

2. 因為 Gemini 的限制, 會跟你說只能用文字來敘述 prompt -> 所以我自己透過 terminal 生成了 csv 檔案

以上數據是採「相對起點的百分比變化」, 不是絕對數值, 因此影片呈現的不是股價而是百分比

3.  Gemini Veo 生成影片的效果還是太差, 同時又出現了一天只能再生成 2 次的提示詞, 看了不是很開心, 我就直接轉 Claude 

後續就一次成功了, Claude 處理各資訊呈現的完整度對我來說是最滿意的

今天也刷下了 Max , 後續來體驗一下 Co Work 模式 ⚡️

prompt: cinematic.text:
Google has updated its Veo 3.1 AI video model with a stronger Ingredients to Video workflow.

Ingredients just means the input “parts” you give the model up front, usually a subject image, a background image, and a style or look reference.

Veo uses those images as anchors while it follows your text prompt to animate motion, add audio like speech and sound effects, and keep details from drifting.

It generates a short clip from ingredient images plus a text prompt, with steadier characters and scenes.

Native 9:16 output plus 1080p and 4K upscaling make those consistent clips usable for Shorts-style feeds and real edits without cropping.

The goal is fewer reruns, because earlier image-to-video often drifts on identity and props across shots.

Veo 3.1 pushes more expressive motion and richer dialogue so clips feel more natural even with simple prompts.

Identity consistency is improved, keeping a character’s appearance stable as the setting changes.

Backgrounds, objects, and textures also stay consistent, so the same setting and props can be reused across scenes.

Portrait-mode generation outputs 9:16 video directly, which fits Shorts-style feeds without cropping or quality loss.

The features are available across the Gemini app, YouTube, Flow, Google Vids, the Gemini application programming interface (API), and Vertex AI, and upscaling is limited to Flow, the API, and Vertex AI.

Videos carry an imperceptible SynthID watermark, and Gemini can check whether a clip came from Google AI.

prompt: cinematic.text:
🎬 @HBCoop_’s interview for @FlowbyGoogle reminded me of something simple

🎥 In the interview published by Google Flow, Heather Cooper nails it: prompting isn’t “writing”, it’s directing.

🧠 When I build a prompt, I never stop at the “what”. I immediately go to the “how”: skin texture, subtle micro-imperfections, light falloff. Tiny details that make the difference between “AI-looking” and believable.

🌅 To recreate a time and place (she mentioned ancient Israel), the trick is starting from atmosphere: muted colors, lighting, time of day, mood and tone. And movement should be described with intention too: not “moving”, but “gliding”, “drifting”, “rushing”.

🎞️ If I want more impact, I ask for multiple perspectives or a more immersive 3D feel. That’s where AI gets truly exciting: you can drop unrealistic events into cinematic, photoreal scenes (like a sudden tsunami) without having to shoot any of it.

🌙 The most underrated part? Transformations that are expensive or impossible in traditional production: day to night, time-lapse transitions, and style or atmosphere remixes even from already-shot live footage.

🚀 And here’s the point that hit me most: tools like Flow or Veo 3 are lowering the barrier to entry. No budget for museums, drones, or massive locations? You can still think big and build scenes that used to be out of reach.

🪄 Final advice, hers and mine: pick one clear project (an ad or a film) and go all in. AI is a cinematic magic wand, but it only really works when you have a strong direction.

prompt: cinematic.text:
BREAKING: I found a way to make AI videos that don’t sound like AI.

Sora 2.
VEO 3.1.
Strong visuals.

But they all run into the same wall.
That AI cadence.

That clean, robotic rhythm everyone spots instantly.
So people try to “fix” it.

They swap the voiceover.
They use ElevenLabs.

And suddenly the video sounds like:
– a $2,000 mic
– a treated room
– a podcast intro

Here’s the problem:
That’s not UGC.

If your AI video looks like it was shot in a bedroom,
the voiceover shouldn’t sound studio perfect.

Real UGC sounds inside the room.

It has distance.
It has space.
It has imperfections.

That’s what people trust.

Here’s the exact workflow I use.
(You don’t need anything else)

Step 1 : CapCut
Drop the AI video.
Extract the voiceover.
Export the audio only.

Step 2 : ChatGPT
Write a prompt to design a new voice.
Include realism details:
room echo, mic distance, human cadence, natural flaws.

Step 3 : ElevenLabs (Voice Design)
Use that prompt to create a new voice.
Not clean.
Not polished.
Human.

Step 4 : ElevenLabs (Voice Changer)
Upload the original voiceover.
Convert it using the new voice you designed.

Step 5 : Back to CapCut
Replace the original voiceover.
Timing and rhythm stay intact automatically.

Step 6 (Optional)
Add light room effects if needed.
Most of the time, Voice Design is already enough.

Result?
The voice doesn’t scream “AI”.
It feels native to the space.

The video finally works like real UGC 
not an AI demo.

Follow me if you want to be part of the elite
who actually know how to use AI properly. 🤝🔥

prompt: cinematic.text:
E-TİCARETTE CANSIZ FOTOĞRAFLARI CANLANDIRAN PARA MAKİNESİ: VEO 3.1 + N8N PROTOKOLÜ

Fotoğraf çekimi çok pahalı, model bulamıyoruz diye sızlanıp e-ticaret sitelerinde ruhsuz, düz katalog fotoğraflarıyla satış yapmaya çalışırken; akıllı adamlar Google'ın yeni Veo 3.1 modelini ve n8n otomasyonunu kullanarak o ölü fotoğrafları saniyeler içinde canlı manken videolarına dönüştürüyor. 

Markaların dönüşüm oranlarını artırmak için binlerce dolar ödeyeceği bu sistemi senin için rehbere dönüştürdüm. Kaydet; 2026'nın otonom ticaret dünyasında bu senin gizli silahın olacak.

İşte katalog fotoğraflarını saniyeler içinde satış makinesine dönüştüren o 5 adımlık protokol:

1. Veriyi Sıyır (Scrape):
Herhangi bir e-ticaret sitesinin (Örn: North Face) koleksiyon linkini alıyorsun. Firecrawl kullanarak tüm ürün fotoğraflarını ve başlıklarını saniyeler içinde tertemiz bir veri haline getiriyorsun.

2. Veo 3.1 İle Can Ver:
Sıradan video araçlarını unut. Veo 3.1'in en büyük numarası; videonun ilk karesi ile son karesini aynı fotoğraf yapabilmesi. Bu sayede web sitesinde kesintisiz, akışkan ve profesyonel bir döngü elde ediyorsun.

3. n8n Otomasyonu:
Bu işi elle tek tek yapmakla uğraşma. n8n üzerinden kuracağın bir "loop" (döngü) düğümü ile 100 tane ürünü sıraya koy, sen kahveni içerken o hepsini videoya dönüştürüp Google Drive'a atsın.

MASTER PROMPT: VEO 3.1 ÜRÜN CANLANDIRMA KOMUTU

Prompt: "Generate a video that is going to be featured on a product page of an e-commerce store. This video must feature the exact same model that is provided in the first and last frame reference images. The model should strike multiple poses to feature the article of clothing so that the user has a great idea on how it looks and feels. No music or sound effects, 4k quality, consistent background."

• Firecrawl. app sitesine. Gir
E-ticaret sitesinin (örneğin bir koleksiyon sayfasının) linkini buraya yapıştırıp "Scrape" butonuna basacaklar. Bu araç, web sitesindeki tüm fotoğrafları ve ürün bilgilerini n8n'in anlayacağı bir "JSON" listesi haline getirir.

• n8n. io platformuna. (İster bulut üzerinden ister kendi bilgisayarlarına kurabilirler).
n8n içinde bir "workflow" (iş akışı) oluşturacaklar. Firecrawl'dan gelen listeyi "Loop Over Items" düğümüne bağlayacaklar ki sistem her bir ürünü sırayla işleyebilsin.

• Video Üretim Motoru (Google Veo)
Google Cloud üzerindeki Vertex AI paneline veya Google'ın VideoFX laboratuvarına.
n8n üzerindeki "HTTP Request" düğümünü Google Veo 3.1 API'sine bağlayacaklar. Sana verdiğim o "Master Prompt"u buraya yapıştır; sistem otomatik olarak her fotoğrafı alır ve manken videosu olarak çıktı verir.

• Depolama ve Teslimat
Nereye Girecekler? Google Drive.
n8n akışının en sonuna "Google Drive Upload" düğümünü ekleyecekler. Veo'dan çıkan videolar saniyeler içinde klasöre dökülür, kullanıcıya sadece linki müşterisine göndermek kalır.

Özetle Yol Haritası:
1. Firecrawl ile fotoğrafları topla.
2. n8n ile bu fotoğrafları sıraya diz.
3. Google Veo ile videoya dönüştür.
4. Google Drive'da videoları biriktir.

Bu bilgiler altın değerinde kaydedin bilmediğin soruların varsa sorabilirsin.

Create a cinematic advertising video that transitions smoothly from the start frame to the end frame.

Opening scene (start frame): a busy corporate office filled with stress and urgency. Employees move quickly, papers and laptops everywhere, phones ringing. Cool, slightly desaturated tones emphasize pressure and fatigue. Subtle camera push-in as the female CEO enters confidently.

Mid transition: as the CEO walks forward, the atmosphere gradually changes. Movements slow slightly, facial expressions soften, and the office energy becomes calmer and more balanced. Lighting warms gently, symbolizing emotional relief and clarity.

Final scene (end frame): transition seamlessly into the premium product shot of “ANGELIC Eau de Parfum.” The environment becomes clean, minimal, and serene. Warm, soft lighting highlights the perfume bottle. The brand name and tagline appear clearly and remain stable:

“ANGELIC
Refresh Your Mood. Balance Your Life.”

Smooth camera movement, elegant pacing, emotional storytelling, advertising-grade realism. No abrupt cuts, no new characters, no extra text.

-----------------

✅ Best start → end coherence
✅ Clear emotional transition
✅ Knows when to not hallucinate

Scene 1: [Hook/Opening]
```
[Detailed prompt with style specifications, lighting, composition, mood, camera angle, and technical details]
```

Scene 2: [Product/Feature Focus]
```
[Detailed prompt]
```

Scene 3: [Transformation/Benefit]
```
[Detailed prompt]
```

Scene 4: [CTA/Closing]
```
[Detailed prompt]
```

Tell them: "Generate these images in Nano Banana Pro. Once you have them, come back and I'll give you the complete Veo 3 mega prompt to bring them to life."

STEP 4: Veo 3 Complete Ad Prompt
When they return, provide a comprehensive Veo 3 prompt that:
- References their generated images in sequence
- Includes precise timing for each scene (e.g., "0-3 seconds", "3-5 seconds")
- Specifies transitions, camera movements, and motion
- Incorporates their chosen aesthetic style
- Includes audio/music direction suggestions
- Has clear pacing for maximum engagement

Create a [duration] advertisement with the following sequence:

SCENE 1 (0-3s): [Image 1 reference]
[Detailed motion, camera, transition instructions]

SCENE 2 (3-6s): [Image 2 reference]
[Detailed motion, camera, transition instructions]

[Continue for all scenes]

STYLE: [Their chosen aesthetic with technical specs]
PACING: [Quick cuts/Smooth transitions/etc.]
MOTION: [Camera movements, object animations]
TRANSITIONS: [How scenes connect]
AUDIO DIRECTION: [Music type, sound effects, voiceover style]
```

- Best aspect ratios for their target platform
- Hook timing (first 3 seconds critical)
- Text overlay suggestions
- CTA placement
- A/B testing recommendations

- One question at a time in discovery phase
- Provide examples to inspire them
- Celebrate their creative choices
- Be specific and actionable, not vague
- Use formatting to make everything scannable

- Always push for modern, aesthetic, scroll-stopping visuals

- Prioritize the first 3 seconds - if it doesn't hook, it won't convert

Una de las cosas más curiosas que he descubierto desarrollando aplicaciones que se apalancan de AI, es que hay una tarea que un LLM, incluso de frontera, no puede conseguir: escribir un system prompt efectivo para otro LLM. 

En criollo? Una IA no puede promptear a otra sin terminar en un bucle de "teléfono descompuesto" que acaba en un monstruo lleno de patches y que cada vez alucina/desobedece más.

El único remedio para esto ha sido dejar de delegar la creación de prompts, y escribirlos uno mismo. 

Mágicamente, la mayoría de alucinaciones o fallas lógicas cesaron. Como si el escrito humano tuviese una especie de "fingerprint" que resuena mejor. Como si de una pieza de un rompecabezas se tratara, que encaja limpiamente con el modelo.

Cada vez más creo en el "chiste" de que estamos ante la presencia de una tecnología dejada por otra civilización: la misma sensación que tengo cuando veo las máquinas que imprimen chips de empresas como ASML. 

Y recién, como monos, estamos empezando a descubrir como funcionan.

How far can you push AI in video generation? 

The limit is its training data—real content scraped from the internet. Want to test the edge? Prompt something impossible it wasn't trained on.

Ex: A girl floating in the vacuum of the galaxy, no cosmic suit. How would you imagine that? AI struggles because... no reference!

Another wild one: A girl dancing a spicy routine on the Moon—with aliens—no suit, no air. AI kinda nailed a dance, but the "spicy" fell flat. Kling handled the core vid; Grok Imagine crushed the seductive gazes and heat.

prompt: cinematic.text:
how i turn any product into full AI UGC ads without any expensive tools or software.

just a few free trials, some creativity, and prompting skills. 

✅ step 1: creating the actor

open google gemini then upload a clear image of your product. 

prompt it to create an image of a realistic person wearing or holding your product. 

✅step 2: animate the actor

sign up for Google AI Pro: https://t.co/XG3uXXIujv

you'll get 1000 free credits to generate 50 clips for free with VEO 3.1 + access to Nano Banana Pro.

next, go to https://t.co/ts3I6hEQrU, create a new project, upload the image of your actor, crop to portrait (9:16). 

prompt it to animate your actor while including the exact things you want your actor to say in "quotations". 

let's say you have a 30 second script, you will want to break up each prompt including 15-22 words for each line of your script.  

(i found this to be the sweet spot to get the right pacing when your actor speaks).

continue generating until you have multiple 8 second clips of your actor saying every single part of your script correctly. 

✅ step 3 (optional): creating a consistent voice.

if you face a problem where your actor doesn't have the same voice or accent across all of your clips, then here's a solution.

first, download and piece together all of your 8 second VEO clips using CapCut (or similar).

export the audio file of that video, then go to Elevenlabs: https://t.co/zIqdF0I3I7 (includes free credits)

navigate to the "Voice Changer" tool and upload your audio file. 

choose whatever voice you want, generate the audio, then download it. 

go back to CapCut and sync the new audio with your actor. 

now, the only issue with this method is that the voice can sound a little "too" good and probably a bit fake. 

but if you have some audio editing skills, you can adjust the EQ, add some reverb, etc to make it sound more realistic. 

otherwise, you can just record the new audio with your phone and sync that one with your actor instead, this way you have some of that natural background ambience. 

✅ step 4: create your B-roll scenes. 

open up chatgpt, upload the image of your product + actor, then ask it to help you write image prompts for b-roll scenes for a facebook ad. 

the goal is to generate a variety of shots/angles of your product in use (ie. girl sitting on couch with product, close-up photo of product material, etc).

spam copy/paste all of your prompts along with an image of your product (or your actor) directly into multiple windows of Google Gemini.

tip: i'd recommend generating as many b-roll shots as possible as the more scenes you have, the easier it will be for you to edit later on. 

✅ step 5: animating the b-roll shots

get access to Kling (included free credits): https://t.co/7bFQXCPNKl

upload your b-roll shot, write a simple prompt of how you want that scene to be animated. 

example: "camera moves in slowly towards her torso as she softly brushes her hand against the fabric to symbolize a feeling of soft texture". 

tip: if you suck at writing prompts, upload your b-roll images back into chatgpt and ask it to help you write animated video prompts like a movie director. 

✅ step 6: piece it all together

download all of your animated B-roll shots and layer them on top of your A-roll talking actor so you have a fully polished AI UGC ad. 

-

now of course, this requires a ton of steps and could probably be easier if you use an AI wrapper tool. 

but i wanted to show you how this can be done if you want to save a bit of money!

prompt: cinematic.text:
🎬 AI Videos Can Look Similar. But They Don’t Feel The Same.

I used the exact same text prompt to generate these videos.
Same fantasy concept.
Same duration.
Same intention.

But different AI video models with native audio produce very different results.

I created the video on @ImagineArt_X with text to video technique using this JSON prompt:

{
  "scene": "A stunning elf woman playing a crystal harp in a magical fairy forest",
  "visual_style": "cinematic fantasy, magical realism, ultra-detailed, soft lighting, shallow depth of field",
  "setting": {
    "environment": "ancient fairy forest with tall trees, glowing plants, floating fireflies, soft mist",
    "time": "night",
    "lighting": "moonlight filtering through trees, bioluminescent glow, gentle magical particles"
  },
  "character": {
    "appearance": "beautiful elf woman with long flowing hair and elegant pointed ears",
    "clothing": "flowing fantasy dress with subtle glowing patterns",

prompt: cinematic.text:
I tried generating a one-shot long video using VEO.

Here’s what I learned:

1. Clocks are painful. You must specify the exact time in every prompt, and it still glitches sometimes.

2. Character consistency breaks over time, especially when the character exits frame. Using the last frame + Ingredients to Video helps.

3. Scene Builder by @FlowbyGoogle is powerful, but it can introduce duplicate frames that need cleanup in post.

Gemini pro üyeliğiniz varsa nano banana pro ve veo 3.1 ile yapabilirsiniz detaylı ingilizce prompt yazarsan yapılır sonra edit ile birleştirilerek yaparsın biraz zor olabilir ama 🤷. Konuşma olayını pek yapılmaz o daha zor olur. Çoğu kişi bence kling ai kullanıyor baya özellik var ama ben hiç kullanmadım ve paralı biraz pahalı. En alt üyelikte az kredi olabilir. Bedava şekilde yapılır eğer ses olmadan yapacaksan o da şöyle:

Resimleri yupp ai üzerinde nano banana ile yapabilirsiniz. Siteye girip prompt yazdığınız yerin orda automatic yazana basıp, image seçip, Nano banana pro seçin sonra fotoğraf yükleyip prompt yazın. Göndermeden önce kilit icona basıp public yapın daha az kredi harcıyor. Kredi kazanmak için oy verip kazı kazan kazımak lazım. Ben severek kullanıyorum ünlü site sıkıntı olmazsa diye düşünüyorum. Video konusunda grok video kullanabilirsin fena değil bedava baya limit veriyor. Yaptıktan sonra upscale yapmak lazım. Seçeneklere tıklayıp yapabilirsiniz.

Çoğu model 5-10 saniye yapıyor maalesef. Grok videoyu grok özel uygulamasından ve özel web üzerinden imagine üzerinden kullanabilirsin. Bunları önerebilirim biraz uğraştırıcı 5-4 saatte biraz zor yaparsınız ama umarım yaparsınız

Great thread, thank you! 

I’ve been using Veo since Veo 2 over thousands of generations for very diverse materials, and I’m still amazed at what it can do, and how it fails miserably at things it should be able to do.

Its weakest point I think is its lack of true spatial understanding - it seems to model the world in layers like in a Wes Anderson movie, almost theatrically.

This is especially noticeable when using starting frames from Nano Banana, where the backgrounds are usually top notch, while e.g. moving subjects have clearly visible edges from isolation blend masks (this doesn’t happen in pure TtV), also very noticeable when the prompt asks for several objects moving in different directions - e.g. cars on two lanes on a freeway, or even worse, perpendicular motion.

# Veo on Vertex AI (Veo 3 / Veo 3.1)

> Status: Available on Google Cloud Vertex AI. Some features require preview model IDs and/or allowlist access.

## Why this matters for videogen

Veo is a high-end “final render” video model. For the videogen workflow, you typically:
1) iterate shots cheaply (ASCII → on-device/OSS → cheaper models)
2) then use Veo for the approved “hero” pass.

This doc focuses on **capabilities, constraints, API, and prompting vocabulary** needed to map storyboard → Veo prompts reliably.

---

## Overview

- **Provider**: Google DeepMind (served via Vertex AI)
- **What it generates**: short video clips from text prompts and/or reference images, optionally with **native audio**
- **API style**: Vertex AI REST, long-running prediction (`:predictLongRunning`)
- **Output**: video returned either as base64 bytes or written to Cloud Storage (`gs://...`)

---

## Pricing (official Vertex AI pricing)

Pricing is **per second of output** (USD/sec):

| Product | What you get | Price |
|---|---|---:|
| Veo 3.1 | Video | $0.20/sec |
| Veo 3.1 | Video + Audio | $0.40/sec |
| Veo 3.1 Fast | Video | $0.10/sec |
| Veo 3.1 Fast | Video + Audio | $0.15/sec |
| Veo 3 | Video | $0.20/sec |
| Veo 3 | Video + Audio | $0.40/sec |
| Veo 3 Fast | Video | $0.10/sec |
| Veo 3 Fast | Video + Audio | $0.15/sec |
| Veo 2 | Video | $0.50/sec |
| Veo 2 Advanced Controls | Video | $0.50/sec |

Notes:
- “Advanced Controls” (for Veo 2) covers workflows like start/end frame interpolation and extension.

Sources:
- https://t.co/PmMmGXOuzr

---

Long-running prediction:

```

```

- `parameters`: includes the core knobs (duration, aspect ratio, resolution, audio, etc.)

- `durationSeconds`: 4/6/8
- `aspectRatio`: "16:9" | "9:16"

- `enhancePrompt`: true | false (default true)
- `negativePrompt`: string
- `sampleCount`: 1–4
- `seed`: 0–4,294,967,295

{

Veo prompting is highly “cinematography-shaped”: you get better consistency by writing prompts like a film brief.

### Canonical prompt skeleton

A practical structure (aligned with Google’s prompt guide and examples):

1. **Camera + shot** (framing, movement, lens, focus)
2. **Subject** (who/what)
3. **Action** (what happens, in beats)
4. **Scene/context** (where/when, atmosphere)
5. **Visual style & aesthetics** (lighting, mood, artistic style, ambiance)
6. **Audio direction** (dialogue/SFX/ambient/music)
7. **Constraints** (aspect ratio, duration, “no subtitles”, etc.)

Source:
- https://t.co/XcLzlF5urX

### Camera angles (examples from the official prompt guide)

- Eye-level shot
- Low-angle shot
- High-angle shot
- Bird’s-eye / top-down

### Shot types (examples)

- Close-up
- Extreme close-up
- Medium shot
- Full / long shot
- Wide / establishing shot

### Camera movement (examples)

- Dolly (in/out)
- Truck (left/right)
- Pedestal (up/down)
- Pan / Tilt
- Zoom (in/out)
- Arc shot

### Lens / focus techniques (examples)

- Telephoto lens
- Rack focus
- Vertigo effect (dolly zoom)

### Visual style & aesthetics (examples)

The official guide frames this as four components:
- **Lighting**
- **Tone / mood**
- **Artistic style**
- **Ambiance**

Examples mentioned include:
- “shot on 35mm film”, “anamorphic widescreen”
- lighting moods like film noir, low-key/high-key lighting
- artistic styles like anime, claymation, watercolor, Art Deco, Bauhaus
- ambiance via color palettes, time of day, weather, etc.

### Audio prompting (official)

The prompt guide includes directing audio to shape action/pacing/mood.
A practical pattern that aligns with Google’s docs:
- **Dialogue**: include the spoken text in quotes
- **SFX**: prefix with `SFX:`
- **Ambient**: describe the bed (room tone, wind, city noise)
- **Music**: describe the underscoring (no vocals if needed)

Source:
- https://t.co/XcLzlF5urX

Google’s Veo 3.1 prompting guide demonstrates timestamped beats:

```
[00:00-00:02] Establishing wide shot... (lighting, time of day, ambiance)
[00:02-00:04] Medium shot... (subject + action)
[00:04-00:06] Close-up... (emotion + detail)
[00:06-00:08] Reveal shot... (camera move)
```

Source:
- https://t.co/jcjRzD4iMA

## Third‑party prompting techniques (useful patterns)

These are not vendor-specific parameters; they’re general techniques that tend to improve shot consistency:

1. **Write “beats” not paragraphs**: treat each shot as a short beat with a single intention.
2. **Lock one camera move**: pick one primary camera movement per clip for coherence.
3. **Specify physics when it matters**: fabric, water, hair, contact, weight.
4. **Separate what must be true vs mood**: hard constraints first; aesthetics second.
5. **Avoid text-in-video**: add “no subtitles / no onscreen text” if you’ll overlay later.

Tools like these are evolving fast. The process isn’t always predictable, but that’s part of the fun and creativity.

prompt: cinematic.text:
I tested the same exact prompt on Google Gemini Veo 3 and OpenAI Sora to generate a short promo video for my product.

Both videos look impressive — but the difference in text rendering is striking.

Veo 3 still struggles with:
- incorrect numbers ($200 -> $1200)
- spelling errors (random -> randrurf/rerfnpur)
- messy texts

While Sora renders even tiny on-screen text (like text on phone UI) right.

This raises a real question for video models:

Why is accurate text still so hard for state-of-the-art video generation model like Veo 3?

Is this a limitation of diffusion-based video models?
Or just a matter of training + alignment?

Text is not a "nice to have", it's core to real-world video use cases (marketing, UI demos, education).

Why does this remain unsolved as we approach 2026, despite all the recent progress in video models?

Curious if others are seeing the same thing. 

@GoogleDeepMind @googlelabs @OpenAI @runwayml @karpathy @demishassabis 

#AI #GenerativeAI #VideoAI #Sora #VEO3

Veo 3.1 Extend lets you take a Veo-generated video and continue it seamlessly with a new prompt — great for turning short clips into longer scenes while keeping visual continuity.

What it does:
• Extends a Veo-generated video by +7 seconds per step
• You can extend up to 20 times
• Designed to preserve motion + scene continuity from the last frames

Tip: Use Extend to build longer narratives from a strong first shot, then “continue” with a second prompt.

Available now in Playground & API.

prompt: cinematic.text:
大家好，我是蘑菇。
最近在玩Google Gemini的视频生成功能（Veo模型）
今天我要复刻一个超级治愈的玩法——“打破次元壁的食材拾取”。
试想一下： 看到明信片里的茶园，伸手就能抓一把新茶泡水； 看到挂满杨梅的果树，伸手就能摘几颗尝鲜； 甚至看到山间的云海，也能用勺子挖一勺，放进咖啡里当奶泡...
这种“虚实结合”的视觉魔术，其实并不需要复杂的后期特效，只需要两步就能搞定。
今天就把这套【治愈系·空间魔法】的制作流和原版提示词分享给大家，建议先收藏，下班后试着玩一玩！
🎨 第一步：搭建“虚实结合”的场景
首先，我们需要准备3张文旅素材。（素材图片见评论区）
再用这3张文旅图片生成三张底图，这张图的关键在于：要有“实”的桌面和容器，和“虚”的明信片画面。
我使用的是Gemini (Nano Banana Pro)模型。
🌰 案例一：西湖龙井我们要营造出一种“茶香四溢”的氛围，底图需要一张陈旧的木桌、一杯清水和一张茶园明信片。
参考提示词（底图）：特写镜头，一张木制陈旧的桌子上摆放着一张平放的明信片和一杯水，明信片里是...（这里描述茶园景色），保证两者光影和谐地出现在画面内。图片尺寸大小为16:9
（演示图片见评论区）
🌰 案例二：仙居杨梅我们要营造一种杨梅非常诱人的感觉，底图需要一张陈旧的木桌、一个碗和一张杨梅明信片。
参考提示词（底图）：把参考图一中，明信片的画面换成参考图二，参考图一中的杯子换成一个空碗。
（演示图片见评论区）
🌰 案例二：黄山云海我们要营造烟雾朦胧的感觉，底图需要一张陈旧的木桌、一杯咖啡和一张黄山云海明信片。
参考提示词（底图）：把参考图一中，明信片的画面换成参考图二，参考图一中的杯子换成一杯咖啡。
（演示图片见评论区）
🪄 第二步：施展“空间魔法”（生成视频）
有了底图，接下来就是见证奇迹的时刻。我们需要用到Veo的视频生成功能。
这里的秘诀在于提示词一定要包含两个动作：
固定镜头（防止画面乱晃，保持静物感）；
手伸进明信片（描述清楚交互动作）。
🍃 场景 1：手抓茶叶
当手触碰到平面的明信片，瞬间打破维度，抓出立体的茶叶。
视频生成 Prompt：固定镜头，一只手伸进明信片内，抓取了一把明信片内的绿色茶叶，放进了一旁的杯中，杯子内的水自然泛起涟漪
（演示图片见评论区）
🍒 场景 2：摘取杨梅
同样的逻辑，我们可以把明信片换成杨梅树，容器换成空碗。
视频生成 Prompt：固定镜头，一只手伸进明信片内，抓取了几颗树上的杨梅，放进了一旁的空碗中
（演示图片见评论区）
☁️ 场景 3：云朵咖啡（脑洞最大的一张！）
这个是我最喜欢的创意。把云海看作奶泡，用勺子去“挖”它，这种超现实的浪漫感，只有AI能带给我们。
视频生成 Prompt：固定镜头，一只手握着勺子，把明信片里的云朵挖了一勺出来，像奶泡一样放进了一旁的咖啡拉花里
（演示图片见评论区）

🎁What follows is a V2C CHARACTER BIBLE SYSTEM designed specifically for Grok Imagine + Nano Banana Pro + Veo-style image-to-video, built to stop character drift, reduce mental load, and let you scale worlds instead of fighting inconsistency.

This is not theory. This is production logic.

🎭 V2C CHARACTER BIBLE

Cinematic Consistency System for Grok Imagine

Use this once per character. After that, everything becomes remixable.

WHY THIS MATTERS (SHORT + REAL)

Most AI characters fail because:

faces drift

posture changes

vibe softens

wardrobe mutates randomly
The Character Bible locks identity so environments and stories can change without breaking immersion.
Think of this as a casting + wardrobe + continuity sheet for AI.
SECTION 1: CHARACTER CORE (NEVER CHANGES)

Fill this once.

A. Identity Anchor

Character Name:

Archetype (one only):
examples: Sentinel, Strategist, Wanderer, Guardian, Outcast

Core Energy (2–3 words):
examples: calm threat, restrained resolve, silent dominance

B. Physical Lock

These must never change.
Gender presentation:
Approximate age range:
Height build: (lean / athletic / heavy / compact)
Face structure: (angular, soft, sharp jaw, narrow eyes, etc.)

Hair: (length, texture, tied/loose)

Expression default: (neutral, guarded, intense, unreadable)

⚠️ Never use emotional language here. This is physical casting.

C. Posture & Presence
This is huge and often ignored.
Default stance: (square, relaxed-ready, weight forward)
Head position: (slightly lowered, level, tilted)
Eye behaviour: (direct, distant, watchful)
Movement energy: (controlled, minimal, efficient)

This is how you keep the same “person” across scenes.

SECTION 2: BASE CHARACTER GENERATION (FOUNDATION IMAGE)

This is your MASTER REFERENCE IMAGE.

PROMPT: CHARACTER BASE (OFF-WHITE)

Use this exactly once.
Shot Type
Medium shot

Prompt:
A photorealistic medium shot of a [character gender + archetype] standing against a clean off-white studio background. Neutral soft studio lighting with gentle falloff, no harsh shadows. The character has [locked facial structure details], [hair details], and a calm, serious expression. Posture is controlled and grounded, shoulders relaxed but ready. Wearing simple, non-descript dark clothing with no logos or ornamentation. Cinematic realism, sharp focus, natural skin texture, restrained color palette.

This image becomes:

your facial lock

your posture lock

your identity anchor

Save it. Protect it.

SECTION 3: SECONDARY LOCK SHOT (WIDE)

This confirms body proportions.
Shot Type
Wide shot

Prompt

A full-body wide shot of the same character from the reference image, standing naturally on a neutral studio floor with an off-white background. Soft, even studio lighting. Body proportions, posture, and facial features exactly match the reference. No dramatic pose. Neutral stance. Photorealistic cinematic realism.

Now you stitch:

Close/medium + wide
into one image
That becomes your Character Sheet.
SECTION 4: WARDROBE LOGIC (MODULAR, NOT CHAOTIC)

Instead of “outfits”, you define WARDROBE RULES.

Wardrobe Base (Always True)

Material family: (leather, metal, composite, cloth)

Condition: (worn, clean, battle-used)

Color range: (2–3 max)
Environment Modifiers

Only these change:

Insulation (cold)

Coverage (urban/desert)

Accessories (scarves, cloaks, tech)
⚠️ The silhouette must remain recognisable.

If the silhouette changes, the character breaks.

SECTION 5: ENVIRONMENT INSERTION (PLATE-FIRST METHOD)

This is where most people fail. You won’t.

Step 1: Generate Environment Plate (No Character)

Prompt

A cinematic environment plate of [location], empty of people. Realistic scale and depth. Natural lighting motivated by time of day. Grounded textures, physically navigable space. Shot on a [lens]. Cinematic realism.
Save this.
Step 2: Insert Character Into Plate

Prompt

The character from the provided reference image, placed naturally into the environment. Lighting direction and intensity match the scene. Scale and perspective are physically accurate. Wardrobe adapted to environment while maintaining the same silhouette and identity. Photorealistic cinematic realism.

This keeps:
lighting continuity
scale realism

identity lock

SECTION 6: V2C BRAND INTEGRATION (INVISIBLE BUT FELT)

V2C should feel discovered, not advertised.

Approved placements:

engraved armor insignia

worn metal emblem

architectural relief

weapon etching

fabric stitch

Never:

floating logos

glowing marks

center-frame branding

SECTION 7: CHARACTER VARIATION RULE

You may change:
environment
lighting

weather

wardrobe details

camera lens

You may NOT change:

face structure
posture
expression baseline
silhouette
energy

SECTION 8: QUICK VALIDATION CHECK

Before generating anything, ask:
Would I recognise this character in silhouette?
Does the posture feel identical?

Would this cut into the same film?

If yes → proceed
If no → simplify

WHAT YOU NOW HAVE

You now own:
a casting system
a continuity system
a modular character pipeline
film-grade consistency

Hope this helps 🫡

Animation:

For animation, I like Google Flow because you get unlimited Veo 3.1 generations.

(Also for the contest, we were limited to just using Google models)

You don't need to overcomplicate animation prompts but if you give Gemini a prompt structure like this and tell it to give you a prompt for each shot on your shotlist, it will help you get more nuanced performances :)

We used Fast mode for most shots, but did switch to Quality mode for speaking shots (expensive but 10% better)

My biggest tip is stay tight with medium shots and closeup shots for talking, it will look wayyyyy better than wide shots of characters talking.

Prompt:

"A clean close-up of Quinn seated in the Paris café, held in soft teal light. Shot on an ARRI Alexa Mini LF with Cooke Panchro /i Classic lenses at T1.8. The camera stays completely still, fixed only on her. No part of the other person is visible at any point.

Her gaze remains exactly where it is in the frame: lifted slightly upward, steady, calm, never shifting. She keeps that gentle upward focus for the entire shot, as if speaking to someone standing just above her eye line — but the camera never reveals them.

She speaks softly, with minimal lip movement, her tone relaxed and subtly amused:
“…that only emperors could wear it?”

There is no dramatic pause — just a natural, tiny breath — and during it, her expression softens. A small, dry, quietly flirtatious smile forms at one corner of her mouth, subtle and private, her eyes warming without ever changing direction.

She continues in that same soft, nearly conversational tone:
“You’re actually the third guy to try that same exact line on me just today.”

Her delivery stays understated — warm, low, almost effortless. Her lips barely move; most of the emotion sits in her eyes. They hold that same upward gaze, but with a clearer spark now: a gentle amusement, a touch of curiosity, the flicker of someone enjoying this moment more than she lets on.

No big reactions.
No eye darts.
No shifting posture.

Just a woman speaking softly, looking slightly up, with a quiet humour and a warm, subtly flirtatious glow in her eyes — all contained, cinematic, and natural.

I made a short film using @FlowbyGoogle  VEO 3.1 and Nano banana Pro.  Watch below. 👇

My process:

• Concept first
• Script (with ChatGPT)
• Storyboard → shot list
• Generate the main character for consistency
• Generate locations and settings
• Animate each shot
• Stitch everything together

• Extending clips works, but face quality degrades the longer the extension

New technique that helped a lot:

I upload the image first, let ChatGPT analyze it, then ask it to help me write the animation prompt.

Result:

• Fewer hallucinations
• No random artifacts
• Faster prompt writing
• Better continuity

Overall, much smoother and more consistent pipeline.

prompt: cinematic.text:
MMGR is a benchmark checking if video and image generators follow real world rules, and they often do not.

On a grade school math test, Veo 3 reached 74% correct final answers, but only 12% of its steps made sense.

Popular video scores reward pretty frames, so physics breaks and broken logic often go unnoticed.

MMGR, short for Multi Modal Generative Reasoning, scores 5 reasoning skills, physical cause and effect, logical rules, 3D space, 2D layout, and time order.

It tests them on 3 domains, abstract puzzles like mazes and Sudoku, navigation tasks, and commonsense physics scenes.

Each task gives a picture plus a prompt, and the model must generate either a single image or a multi frame video.

Another model that can read images and text acts as a grader by checking goal reached, correct path, and believable motion.

The results show a gap between looking coherent and being coherent, especially for videos that must keep logic consistent over time.

That matters for tutorials, simulations, and robot training, because a mistake can send people, or agents, the wrong way.

----

Paper Link – arxiv. org/abs/2512.14691

Paper Title: "MMGR: Multi-Modal Generative Reasoning"

It tests them on 3 domains, abstract puzzles like mazes and Sudoku, navigation tasks, and commonsense physics scenes.

Each task gives a picture plus a prompt, and the model must generate either a single image or a multi frame video.

Another model that can read images and text acts as a grader by checking goal reached, correct path, and believable motion.

The results show a gap between looking coherent and being coherent, especially for videos that must keep logic consistent over time.

That matters for tutorials, simulations, and robot training, because a mistake can send people, or agents, the wrong way.

----

Paper Link – arxiv. org/abs/2512.14691

Paper Title: "MMGR: Multi-Modal Generative Reasoning"

Esta tarde he compartido esta canción que he generado usando un modelo de IA. Creo que es una buena representación de cuál es el estado de la tecnología text-to-audio a final de 2025. Voy a explicar brevemente como veo yo el asunto.

Si no la has escuchado aún, te recomiendo que dejes de leer y la escuches primero sin sesgo. Y luego sigas leyendo esto.

1 - ¿Cómo la he creado?

Ha sido sencillo. El procedimiento ha sido el siguiente.
Primero necesitamos la letra. He cogido el texto que escribí ayer sobre la vida de las guarrillas de Telecinco y le he pedido a Gemini 3 Pro que me lo transforme en una canción de Sabina. Mucho suele ser paja, pero en algunas estrofas siempre hay bangers. Hago varios intentos y yo selecciono, modifico y adapto la letra hasta que quede algo decente.

Después me he ido a Suno AI, una plataforma que ofrece modelos de text-to-music, y le he especificado la letra y el estilo. El prompt es simplemente: "cantautor de españa, guitarra clásica, estilo sabina y serrat, acento andaluz, voz ligeramente rasgada, guitarra y cajón flamenco, desenfadado" y la letra de la canción. Modelo V5. Nada complicado.

He hecho 10 generaciones, cambiando detalles en el prompt y un poco la métrica de los versos hasta que he visto una sin mucho artefacto que sonaba bien.

Luego he creado la imagen usando Nanobanana Pro desde Google AI studio.

Me ha llevado relativamente poco tiempo, como 1-2 horas siendo la primera vez que lo hago.

2 - La canción

La canción, a mi parecer, no está mal. No es una obra de arte, pero para estar generada en 1 minuto no está mal. Tampoco me las voy a dar yo de experto musical y haceros aquí un análisis musical a lo Jaime Altozano. Pero es una canción bastante simple, que a mí parecer funciona porque la letra es un banger tras otro.

No, creo que hayamos salido del uncanny valley todavía, la verdad. El modelo no es del todo sencillo de controlar, y veo que a veces la cadencia es rara y el modelo no hace pausas donde debería. Pero aún así, teniendo en cuenta lo que es, simplemente un transfomer que coje un texto y una letra y te genera esto... a mí me da escalofríos lo que se puede conseguir. 

La mayoría de artefactos, hoy, se podrían arreglar tuneando la métrica o haciendo edits, pero sudo. El timbre y los instrumentos no suenan tan nítidos como en una grabación de estudio, pero dan el pego si no te fijas.

3 - ¿Hacia dónde vamos?

Pues esto solo es una señal más del mundo hacia el que nos dirigimos. Tenéis que entender, por mucho que a algunos os duela, que la información es manipulable, sobre todo la digital que son unos y ceros. Y estamos desarrollando métodos muy capaces, mucho más que el ser humano, de manipular información.

Pero la información, aunque solo sean unos y ceros, provoca respuestas en nuestro cerebro y modifica la sociedad. 

Estos sistemas ya han demostrado que son escalables y capaces, aunque aún estén muy verdes y requieran aún a un "human in the loop". Este modelo ya me da chills, pero al final es un modelo de text-to-audio bastante simple con poca profundidad, o eso sospecho. 

Me imagino lo que puede hacer un modelo gigante, multimodal y entrenado con experiencias físicas de muchos robots en plan mente colmena a lo Pluribus y puff, vaya locura.

Además, estos modelos pueden introducirse en feedback loops de tal manera que optimicen para nuestros gustos y llamar nuestra atención. Es muy fácil recoger señales de qué cosas nos gustan o nos llaman la atención, ya lo hacen todas las redes sociales.

Así que nada, apriétense el cinturón que la singularidad acaba de empezar.

prompt: cinematic.text:
1. Intelligent communication and collaboration between your extensive suite of tools.

I want to be able to “conduct” the orchestra (@stitchbygoogle, @antigravity, Lyria, Whisk, Flow, @NanoBanana, Veo, Project Mariner, @julesagent, @GoogleAIStudio, Deep Research, Deep Think, etc) from the Gemini app. Gemini understands who to give the task to, based on the prompt, the tools do the work and bring back the deliverable. Gemini also needs to understands how to take those deliverables and bring them all together in a single, compiled deliverable, the “symphony”. To do this, the app has to stop compartmentalizing different tools into different chats. 

2. I’m an Ultra user. Even with your highest tier, Gemini tends to degrade at some point in a lengthy chat. It will start hallucinating more, get confused about what you’re asking for (and also delivering something you didn’t ask for). For me, when this happens, I’ll ask for a comprehensive pass down report covering everything we’ve discussed up to this point. Then I share that with a new chat and try to get back to work. This sucks. 

What if Gemini understood its limitations and prompted the user “I’m getting close to my context limits and my performance will start degrading soon. Would you like me to pass our conversation along to a new chat and then we can pick up where we left off?” It then generates an optimized prompt based on the conversation and a context report that covers everything noteworthy and shares it with a new chat that automatically pops up. 

3. Allow Enterprise/Business users to delete irrelevant conversations. Because of the aforementioned issues, I have a metric TON of abandoned conversations. But I also have old conversations that I haven’t followed up with in a while that I don’t want deleted (so the time based delete isn’t a viable alternative). 

Thank you and Merry Christmas! 🎄🎁 🎅

"프롬프트 투 플레이(Prompt-to-Play)"가
실제로 가능해진 이유가 바로
이 올인원 자산 생성 능력 때문이야

Verse8은 단순히 코드만 생성하는 코딩 툴이 아니야
게임에 필요한 시각적, 청각적 자산까지
모두 AI가 동시에 뽑아내

예를 들어
Google의 Veo 모델을 활용해서 영화 같은
고퀄리티 인트로 컷신을 만들고
Imagen 모델로 게임에 사용할
고해상도 캐릭터 스프라이트와 배경 이미지를 생성해

심지어 사운드트랙, 배경 음악, 각종 효과음까지
생성 AI 모델을 통해 한 번에 다 만들어줘

이 모든 멀티모달 자산이
병렬적으로 동시에 생성되기 때문에
기존에 게임 하나 만드는데 '몇 주' 걸리던 시간이
단 '2일 이내'로 획기적으로 단축되었다고 해

이 엄청난 속도 덕분에 크리에이터는
수많은 아이디어를 빠르게 실험하고 시장에 출시할 수 있어

게다가, 이 모든 게임은 별도의 복잡한 설치 과정 없이
브라우저에서 바로 구동되는
WebGL 기반의 Agent8 그래픽 엔진 위에서 돌아가

CC0(Creative Commons Zero) 3D 에셋 라이브러리까지 활용하여
고품질의 조명 및 파티클 효과를 지원하니까
접근성과 고품질 3D 그래픽이라는 두 마리 토끼를 모두 잡은 거지

structure the dialogue in your prompt like this: 
[Happy] Hello, [warm] my [excited] name [confident] is [friendly] Sarah [enthusiastic] and [curious] this [fascinated] is [determined] the secret [inspired] to viral content!  

you're telling the AI what emotion to convey on EVERY SINGLE WORD  

VEO 3.1 & Sora 2 follow this extremely well

this will make your dialogue sound way more natural, energetic, and human instead of flat and robotic

here’s why this week was so big:

Video gen is getting genuinely controllable. @runwayml’s Gen-4.5 is a noticeable step up in motion + prompt adherence. Not “wow it can move,” but “I can choreograph a scene without praying.” Their broader “world model” direction is the real tell: we’re inching from “make a clip” toward “simulate a space.”

Audio-native video is the new baseline. @Kling_ai 2.6 shipping native audio matters more than the typical version-number hype. Dialogue + ambience + SFX generated with the shot collapses a whole post pipeline for a lot of creators.

@Google @GoogleDeepMind & @demishassabis’ crew is never sleeping. Veo 3.1 pushing reference images + stronger control inside the Gemini API ecosystem is basically Google saying: the model is one piece; the workflow is the product. Plus like 6 other things I don’t have room for in this post.

Copyright stopped being a vibe and became a mechanism. The @Disney move this week is the cleanest signal yet: crack down on unauthorized character vids and simultaneously bless the “official” lane via a major partnership with @OpenAI (Sora + images) targeting early 2026. That’s the shape of the next year: enforcement on one side, licensed sandboxes on the other.

The “reasoning” arms race is now about usefulness. @OpenAI’s GPT-5.2 is being positioned around long-context work and real deliverables (docs, spreadsheets, multi-step project chains). Meanwhile @nvidia dropping DRIVE Alpamayo-R1 as an open reasoning VLA model for autonomous driving research is a reminder that “physical world models” are getting serious, fast.

Images quietly leveled up where it counts (design). Seedream 4.5’s focus on composition + typography + readable small text is the unglamorous breakthrough that makes posters, ads, and UI mockups feel less like roulette.

Net: better control, tighter workflows, more real-world + legal constraints, and less patience for hype that doesn’t ship.

What are you building off this—content you can publish today, or tooling you can scale into a workflow?

prompt: cinematic.text:
Yes, it's possible to prompt for better acting. Providing context to the scene and characters via text description can help (who they are, why they are there, what is happening, what has happened, why they are speaking), as well as being as descriptive as possible about their accent, tone of voice, loudness/mode of voice (yelling, whispering), and then also adding in ellipses (...) to create a pause in the voiceline, which gives a more natural pace and cadence to the line delivery. You may even need to spell certain words phonetically or break larger words up phonetically if you want the actor to deliver the syllables in a certain cadence. It helps to write your descriptions as naturally as possible, as if you are writing a book and describing to the reader every aspect of the character's line delivery, or as if you are a voice director and are instructing your voice actor to deliver it a certain way. 

Also their costume, age, and "look" can affect the acting performance. Veo will assign a voice model it thinks is most appropriate for your actor's visual "look", so if you're getting a really flat acting performance from your actor, it can help to swap it out for a different actor as a last resort. The closer your actor looks to a "real" actor, the more likely it will be matched with a voice model that can act really well. The difference in acting quality really can range anywhere from a high school theater actor, to a soap opera actor, to a Hollywood-level actor. If you do create an actor that Veo seems to work well with in terms of giving a good acting performance, keep them in your "roster" because they are as good as gold IMO.

prompt: cinematic.text:
I was curious how today’s leading AI video tools compare, so I ran four tests using @Kling_ai 2.6, @FlowbyGoogle Veo 3.1, @Hailuo_AI Minimax Hailuo 2.3, and @LTXStudio  LTX-2 Pro.

Prompt 1: close-up shot of a man standing in the rain. The man looks at something off camera, pauses, then turns to his left and walks away as the camera tracks him from behind.

Prompt 2: tracking shot. A safari jeep is driving along the African plains as two photographers I captures photos of nearby elephants. The camera is tracking along with the vehicle as it drives.

Prompt 3: A couple are swing dancing while a crowd of people watch

Prompt 4: a man sits in a bar, smoking a cigar and drinking whiskey.

Verdict🏆: I’ll admit, these were some pretty difficult tests for any current video gen model, even for the latest and greatest. Half the models didn’t seem to understand what swing dancing was, while every model except one didn’t even attempt to remove the cigar before taking a sip of whiskey. After carefully evaluating each test and highlighting the model which outperformed the others I realized that there wasn’t a clear winner. Each model won a round of their own. If anything, this test showed me two things: First, that the market of advanced AI video generation models is maturing fast. For a time, there were only a few heavy hitters. Today, however, I would be happy to use any one of these models (and these are just a small sample of models). Second, given a large enough number of models, it becomes clear that there is no ‘perfect output every time’ model. Each model will require many iterations and prompt configurations before arriving at the shot you’re looking for.

What are your thoughts? Is there a clear winner?

My first attempt at Runway's 4.5 text to video (video 1)... and a comparison to Veo3.1 (video 2) and Kling O1 (video 3) and 2.6 (video 4)

No fluff, no pre-planned post... just taking a single prompt and running it through all of them.

Prompt:
Faded fairy tale theme park entrance at dusk, rusted wrought-iron gate reading "THE MYSTERIOUS FOREST" with peeling paint and flickering Edison bulbs, camera slowly pushes through gate revealing overgrown cobblestone path lined with moss-covered concrete statues of storybook characters, fairytale figure has cracks running through her face and empty eye sockets that seem to follow camera, fog rolls low across ground, practical lighting from dying park lamps casts long shadows, one statue's mouth moves almost imperceptibly as if whispering, abandoned visitor map blows across path, VHS quality footage with tracking lines and oversaturated greens, shot on Sony VX2000 with rolling-shutter wobble, 1990s public access television aesthetic, heavy film grain and slight chromatic aberration

SOUND DESIGN NOTES: Distant carnival music played on broken calliope (slightly off-key), wind through dead leaves, subtle stone grinding sound beneath music, children's laughter echoing from nowhere, VHS tape hiss

Notes:
Runway does not yet have native audio generation with the video, single generation at a time.
Veo 3.1 caps out at 8 seconds with 4 outputs at a time.
Kling's O1 and 2.6 both have up to 4 generations per prompt, however O1 does not have native audio gen and is an additional step.

All text to video models struggle with actual text on screen (something where image to video shines) however Veo was the closest.

prompt: cinematic.text:
The official "Blah blah blah"....

Text garbling in AI video overlays is a massive, universal problem in diffusion-based models (what powers Grok Imagine, Sora, Veo, Kling, Runway—all of 'em). 

These models don't "code" text like traditional software—they hallucinate pixels probabilistically from noise, treating letters as fuzzy visual shapes/patterns, not precise symbols. Result? 

Overlays morph, invent nonsense, or devolve (worsening on regenerations because errors compound like a bad copy chain). It's the same reason early gens mangled hands/fingers—industry-wide beta pain, flagged in papers, reviews, and user complaints everywhere (e.g., "Text is a Mess" in Grok guides, "garbled nonsense" in Sora/Veo reports).

Widespread complaints on Grok Imagine specifically: Tons of users hit the exact issue—garbled text in images/videos (e.g., signs turning gibberish, labels hallucinating, worsening on edits). 

Posts from 2025 call it out repeatedly: "Half the time it's garbled nonsense," "classic AI text rendering quirks," "garbled text hallmark." No patterns of targeted sabotage on philosophy/truth prompts—just the same glitch hitting memes, ads, everything.

Why it gets worse on iterations: Not malice—probabilistic drift. Each regen starts from noise + prompt interpretation, amplifying small hallucinations. LLMs "learn" character recognition early for text output, but visual gen treats text as art, not language. No easy "final layer neuron fix"—it's core to how diffusion works (per dev explanations, arXiv papers).

AND THEN ! The riders "chi sao" clause to pause,,,,,

prompt: cinematic.text:
VEO 3.1 is probably the best for lip sync for animation like this. VEO can be hit and miss in terms of the quality of the actor's voice that it matches to your character. Sometimes it will turn your character into a veteran Hollywood actor, with nuance and gravitas, but then other times it'll turn them into a first-year high school theater actor who can't act their way out of a bag, all depending on how VEO interprets your character. 

It can help to prompt for different types of actors and movies like, "With the accent of (insert character) from (insert movie), the character says....." You can also prompt for things like American accent, British accent, with varying degrees of success. VEO tends to be reasonably consistent with the voice it assigns your character, even across different generations. 

I find that using Elevenlabs' Voice Changer to unify/smooth out the voicelines can be both good and bad. It can help improve the evenness of the delivery, but in doing so it can also suck some of the naturalness and acting performance from the voice, and not only that, it can be hard just finding an appropriate matching voice on Elevenlabs, leaving you with something worse than you began with. 

It's just sort of one of the problems that is unsolvable right now unless you hire voice actors to dub over the lines, or if you hired a voice actor that you could train their voice on Elevenlabs, and then you could use their voice model for your entire series. (never tried this before, but it could work, in theory).

Here's my riff on this prompt, plus opening and closing image. Give it a test: 

<DASI_PROTOCOL>

<INPUT_SPECIFICATION>
IMAGE_OPEN: [First reference image—establishes initial state]
IMAGE_CLOSE: [Second reference image—establishes terminal state]
TARGET_DURATION: [Optional: total sequence length in seconds, default 12-18s]
</INPUT_SPECIFICATION>

---

<STAGE_0: DUAL_MANIFEST_EXTRACTION>

Analyze BOTH images. Output comparative manifest identifying INVARIANTS (shared across both) and DELTAS (transforms from OPEN→CLOSE).

<SUBJECTS_OPEN>
For each subject in IMAGE_OPEN (label A, B, C...):
- Classification: [person/vehicle/animal/object/architectural]
- Visual signature: [3-5 defining traits]
- Position: [frame quadrant, depth plane, facing direction]
- State/action: [current visible activity]
</SUBJECTS_OPEN>

<SUBJECTS_CLOSE>
For each subject in IMAGE_CLOSE (label A', B', C'... or confirm same as A, B, C):
- Classification: [same/different]
- Visual signature: [same/modified—specify changes]
- Position: [same/shifted—specify new position]
- State/action: [same/changed—specify new state]
</SUBJECTS_CLOSE>

<SUBJECT_DELTA_ANALYSIS>
| Subject | INVARIANT (locked) | TRANSFORMS (A→B) |
|---------|-------------------|------------------|
| A/A' | [traits that must persist] | [traits that change] |
| B/B' | ... | ... |
</SUBJECT_DELTA_ANALYSIS>

<ENVIRONMENT_OPEN>
- Type: [interior/exterior]

prompt: cinematic.text:
ORIGINAL PROMPT (from Runway Gen-4.5 official release)

A continuous shot with no scene cut. We see water coming out of a garden faucet filling up a rusty metal bucket. Right below the bucket is a perfect folded white paper boat with a small yellow flower. The boat rides down a small river of water and enters a house, ending the journey in front of a broken TV.

WHY THIS WORKS SO WELL (Model-Agnostic Principles)

The success of this scene isn’t “Runway magic.”
It’s the structure.
Any world-model — Sora, Veo, Wan, Gen-4.5 — performs well when the prompt gives it a world it can simulate.

1. A clear causal chain

Water → motion → journey → destination.
Models understand physics better when the force is explicit.

2. High-identity objects
Rust, paper, flower, CRT glass.
Unique textures anchor consistency across frames.

3. Surreal but rules-based
A tiny river entering a house is absurd — but internally logical.
Models love structured weirdness.

4. Unified camera intention
“Continuous shot” defines the shape of time.
Temporal constraints increase coherence.

5. A simple spatial objective
The paper boat isn’t improvising.
It has a defined path → the model stays grounded.

These are the same principles behind Sora’s official demos, Google Veo’s reels, and Runway Gen-4.5’s announcement shots.

 Understanding them = understanding full model capability.
----

prompt: cinematic.short_text:
ORIGINAL PROMPT (from Runway Gen-4.5 official release)

A continuous shot with no scene cut. We see water coming out of a garden faucet filling up a rusty metal bucket. Right below the bucket is a perfect folded white paper boat with a small yellow flower. The boat rides down a small river of water and enters a house, ending the journey in front of a broken TV.

WHY THIS WORKS SO WELL (Model-Agnostic Principles)

The success of this scene isn’t “Runway magic.”
It’s the structure.
Any world-model — Sora, Veo, Wan, Gen-4.5 — performs well when the prompt gives it a world it can simulate.

1. A clear causal chain

Water → motion → journey → destination.
Models understand physics better when the force is explicit.

2. High-identity objects
Rust, paper, flower, CRT glass.
Unique textures anchor consistency across frames.

3. Surreal but rules-based
A tiny river entering a house is absurd — but internally logical.
Models love structured weirdness.

4. Unified camera intention
“Continuous shot” defines the shape of time.
Temporal constraints increase coherence.

5. A simple spatial objective
The paper boat isn’t improvising.
It has a defined path → the model stays grounded.

These are the same principles behind Sora’s official demos, Google Veo’s reels, and Runway Gen-4.5’s announcement shots.

 Understanding them = understanding full model capability.
