prompt: cinematic.text:
With @hedra_labs latest lip-sync update, it lets you feed in a pre-recorded audio clip to generate a performance, so I wanted to see how it holds up against @HeyGen_Official and how both compare to the “video with audio” prompting approach in @FlowbyGoogle VEO 3.1 Fast, @Alibaba_Wan 2.5 Fast, and the new @Kling_ai 2.6.

So I brought in a Nano Banana Pro image of myself and a pre-recorded audio clip, then compared Hedra 3 to the same feature in Heygen. After that, I tried the same audio in VEO 3.1, Wan 2.5 Fast, and Kling 2.6 by prompting with the transcribed text and describing the character talking to himself before asking for coffee.

The results are interesting…

Hedra 3 and Heygen both picked up the emotional tone of the audio, but the output still falls short of feeling human. Hedra 3 still feels robotic and Heygen pushed the expression too far (could an eyebrow rocket upward that much?!). The cool part is they do capture things like pauses and rhythm from the original audio, which gives the performance a bit more shape.

VEO 3.1 and Wan 2.5 don’t let you use your own voice yet, but that actually helps them land more natural movement. VEO, in particular, added non-verbal gestures that support the dialogue, making the performance feel more intentional. Wan 2.5 Fast surprised me with how well it handled eye shifts—down at the book, then up at the camera—with a pretty smooth push-in. The constant jitter in the face was distracting, though. And Kling 2.6, ha well, it tried, and the fact that the model now has audio is huge.

If you asked me, I’d still choose VEO 3.1 to prompt video with audio. It seems like the best approach out there to getting closer to realism.

Curious what you think about these iterations. What’s your preferred method for audio and lip sync right now?

prompt: cinematic.text:
GIỚI THIỆU CẢ NHÀ TRỌN BỘ CÔNG CỤ AI ĐỂ SẢN XUẤT NỘI DUNG VIRAL. 

1. ChatGPT
• Cách dùng: Wording lại bài, viết content, tạo prompt, phát triển kịch bản.
• Ưu điểm: Linh hoạt, nhanh, xử lý mọi dạng nội dung từ ngắn đến dài.

2. Comet
• Cách dùng: Dùng như trình duyệt để quét, thu thập content viral theo trend.
• Ưu điểm: Tự động tổng hợp nội dung hot, siêu tiện để lấy idea.

3. Gemini
• Cách dùng: Tạo ảnh, tạo video, deep research, phân tích tài liệu nặng, làm flashcards, storyboard, tạo gem trợ lý cá nhân,....
• Ưu điểm: Mạnh toàn diện =)) thỉnh thoảng tạo ảnh hơi ng.u, lag,...
4. VEO 3.1

• Cách dùng: Tạo video hoàn chỉnh theo prompt: quảng cáo, animation, phim ngắn,...
• Ưu điểm: Bám prompt cực tốt, dựng được các cảnh phức tạp.
5. Sora 2

• Cách dùng: Tạo source sản phẩm, video quảng cáo nhanh.
• Ưu điểm: Tạo footage chất lượng cao, chuyển động mượt, hợp làm ads.

6. Grok
• Cách dùng: Tạo chuyển động cho ảnh tĩnh, hoặc tạo b-roll nhẹ nhàng cho video.
• Ưu điểm: Animation mềm, hợp cảnh cảm xúc, mood broll, các vid viral của mình hiện tại đều có sự góp mặt của grok trong việc tạo broll minh hoạ.

7. HeyGen
• Cách dùng: Tạo avatar AI, làm video hàng ngày mà không cần quay.
• Ưu điểm: Lip-sync chuẩn, lên video nhanh, nhiều kiểu avatar.

8. Nano Banana Pro
• Cách dùng: Tạo ảnh siêu chân thực, tạo poster, key visual đẹp.
• Ưu điểm: Màu sắc ảo diệu, output đẹp kiểu studio ngay cả với brief đơn giản.

9. Minimax / VBee / 11labs
• Cách dùng: Clone voice cho cá nhân hoặc nhân vật thương hiệu, tạo voice ok.
• Ưu điểm: Giữ được độ tự nhiên, dễ dùng – hoặc dùng Google AI Studio nếu muốn free.

10. Google AI Studio
• Cách dùng: Tạo ảnh, infographic, video, voice, build app,...
• Ưu điểm: Đa nhiệm, miễn phí nhiều tính năng, dễ tích hợp.

11. NotebookLM
• Cách dùng: Upload tài liệu → trích script, tóm tắt → tạo infographic, mindmap, video summary.
• Ưu điểm: Rất mạnh phần nghiên cứu & tổng hợp nội dung thành nhiều format. Mình dùng để trích script, làm content cho kênh.

12. Suno
• Cách dùng: Tạo nhạc nền, nhạc original cho video, jingle thương hiệu.
• Ưu điểm: Nhạc chất lượng cao, tạo mood nhanh, hợp video content.

Cả nhà đang dùng con nào chia sẻ thêm nha. Em thì dùng ChatGPT Plus, Gemini, Veo3, Sora2, CapCut. 

#duongtoolai #aiapp #veo3 #chatgpt #Sora2 #TaiKhoanAI #capcut

prompt: cinematic.text:
With the release of @Kling_ai 2.6, I was eager to put it up against one of its arch-rivals….@FlowbyGoogle Veo 3.1. I ran four separate tests. First, I tested their ability to generate consistent and stable action shots. Second, I tested camera movement in a crowded scene. Third, I tested their ability to generate consistent facial details and emotion. Fourth, I wanted to see how well they can generated an interaction between two characters.

Prompt 1: camera tracking shot, wide-shot. The camera tracks above as two nights ride on horses through a forest. The horses a galloping fast. The camera is tracking the knights from above.

Prompt 2: Slow camera push in on a man eating Ramen at a Ramen house in Japan. The alley street is busy with people.

Prompt 3: Close-up shot of a man on a sailboat. The man has a scared look on his face. After a short pause, the man says, "I'm gonna need a bigger boat”

Prompt 4: Static camera. A man picks up a cookie from a plate and takes a bite. His dog looks up at him; eagerly wanting a bite of the cookie. The man turns, looks at the dog, and says, "no cookies for you mister”

Verdict🏆: To be honest, I was surprised by Kling 2.6. While Veo 3.1 outperformed Kling 2.6 in the close-up shot test, it slightly underperformed in every other test. In the Veo 3.1 outputs, objects would randomly appear and camera movements were abrupt or didn’t adhere to the prompt. Don’t get me wrong, Kling 2.6 definitely had its flaws (its audio was quieter and often mismatched the prompt). That said, I was impressed with Kling 2.6 more than I imagined I would be. Although a somewhat small lead, I would give Kling 2.6 the slight advantage for this round of tests.

prompt: cinematic.text:
I made this film and explained my process during my Twitch stream yesterday:
https://t.co/HEObEnP8Sq

For those who missed it, here is the full breakdown:

🛠️ The Tech Stack:
- Generation: Sora 2 Pro, Veo 3.1, Nano Banana Pro
- Prompting: Kickflix
- Editing: DaVinci Resolve
- Polish: Topaz Video AI (Upscale to 4K) & Epidemic Sound for the SFX

⚙️ The Process:

Concept: 
I used Kickflix to generate the initial prompt variations based on the dystopian concept.

Character Consistency:
The hardest part was keeping the CEO looking the same while talking about different topics. I used the Remix feature in Sora 2 Pro to generate new clips from the original seed, this kept his face consistent while changing the context.

The Horror Elements:
Most of the "B-Roll" was generated in Sora, but I used Nano Banana Pro to generate specific connecting scenes to bridge the gaps between the interview and the background footage.

Assembly:
Stitched everything together in DaVinci Resolve and ran the final export through Topaz to get it crisp at 4K.

Let me know if you have questions about the Remix workflow!

prompt: cinematic.text:
The new King of AI Video just dropped. And it's not from Google or OpenAI.

Yesterday, Runway launched Gen-4.5, and the numbers are ridiculous:
- 1,247 Elo on the Artificial Analysis benchmark
​- Beat Google Veo 3 and OpenAI Sora 2 Pro​
- Same speed and price as Gen-4, but way better quality​

Here's what actually changed:

1. Unprecedented Physical Accuracy
Runway  claims objects now move with "realistic weight, momentum and force" and  liquids finally "flow with proper dynamics." If you've been frustrated  by AI video lacking precision, this is the fix we've been waiting for.
​
2. Built on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs
They  didn't just use NVIDIA chips—they co-engineered the entire stack with  Jensen Huang’s team. From pre-training to inference. This is what  happens when hardware and software teams actually work together.
​
3. The "Success Bias" Bug
My  favorite limitation: If you prompt a missed soccer kick, the model  still makes it score. Why? Because it's trained on successful outcomes.  Runway openly admits this. That's refreshing honesty in an industry full  of hype.
​
The "So What?" for Builders:

The bottleneck isn't quality anymore. It's implementation.

Here is how I’m planning to use Gen-4.5’s 10-second clips in my workflows:

- Landing Pages: Replacing static hero headers with cinematic, 10s loops of "product in action"

- Ads: Generating B-roll for my hooks

- Social: Using the precise camera control (pan, zoom, tilt) to fix specific shots instead of re-generating endlessly.

Availability:
It's rolling out gradually to all users (Standard plan and up) by the end of this week.
​
The tools are ready. How are you going to use them?

prompt: cinematic.text:
Actually you can get the same quality of answers for free via Google AI studio, which offers the latest Gemini Pro series models, but you do get limited use of them and for Nano Banana Pro & Veo 3.1 standard you must pay yourself. Google AI studio is my work horse, because I can adjust the temperature (low temperature for accurate stuff like science, high temperature for creative stuff), system prompt, all those parameters.

And even if you use the free Gemini web service, you can still access Gemini 3.0 Pro. You just need to select as it defaults to Gemini 3.0 Flash, which is a faster, but weaker model.

PS. I don't have paid subscription of Gemini, but Google AI studio is one of my most widely used AI services. I do use it via API as well, built own GUI (similar to ChatGPT, but with more control e.g. you can adjust temperature and system prompt via the web UI on the fly), but that's another story.

🎬[Update 3] - This instrumental music video is basically a short film. Using Google Nano Banana Pro + Veo 3.1 together is interesting combination.

- I do get "Failed Generations" on Google Flow, but not "sensitive content/Policy Restrictions" kind of errors like I have seen before.
- Veo 3.1 video generations are fast! Similar to @grok Imagine.
- Exactly like Grok, Veo 3.1 upscales are equally damaging to details produced in native 720p. But at least it's producing 720p native resolution unlike Grok's 480p. For this reason I'm only taking native 720p videos for editing. Will upscale with @topazlabs after final edit.
- The quality of videos sometimes is great, sometimes "meh", and sometimes "game play" crap instead of cinematic sequences. I have to keep trying editing prompts and images to try to get what I want, and mostly still kinda fail to get. It is time consuming task.
- Ingrediants-to-Video is very useful feature. I am using that more often than frame-to-video. Thanks to @jerrod_lew's recent tweet showing this example.
- Recent <instructions> based keyframe generation prompt from @techhalla is amazingly helpful. I'm using it more often since he showed that method.
- Google AI Studio with Gemini 3 chat for storyboard, text-prompt generation/refinement/enhancements is amazing as well. As equally as @grok's. 👌

I'm happy that I'm kind of learning to get around Google's generative AI tools, which annoyed working with in past music videos. Google tries to play too safe compared to other models.

For this music video I will try my best to stick to Google's models unless somewhere I feel like it's miserably failing at it's task.

High intensity action sequences like fight and two characters doing action scenes are absolute mess. I have to experiment with different models, with different images and prompts. Or maybe has to break down the action equences to even smaller parts and then stitch them together. The morphing between high intensity action scenes is a real trouble, no matter what models I have tried. I believe that's where strong prompting skills shine along with right model. Will try to figure things out as I move forward.

I think this one might also take a week+ time to finish for my slow pace. 😅

3 steps forward... 1 step back. MJ always wants to make fashion model-looking characters (lame), but my bigger issue is more compositional.

When you use classic painterly styles, MJ will fight you when you try to display modern tech. I prompt for a futuristic robotaxi, and I get mostly cars from the 1920s-60s, which means those styles aren't just styles, but they're dragging compositional context baggage with them.

Next gen, smarter "thinking" AI image models should be able to parse art style and compositional context. (this one's going in my next round of feedback in the Veo tester group).

prompt: cinematic.text:
@Kling_ai  and VEO are two of the biggest kids on the block. With Frames to Video in VEO 3.1 being a competitor to Frames in Kling 2.5 Turbo, I wanted to put them to the test to see which one reigns king.

I generated first and last frame images in Midjourney, then brought those into Kling and VEO.

Prompt 1 + Image Inputs: a woman opens a door in front of her and walks through.

Prompt 2 + Image Inputs: a man picks up a sandwich (sitting on a plate in front of him) with both hands and begins eating the sandwich.

Kling - The door test remains illusive for AI, but I was quite impressed with Kling’s ability to understand how doors work. However, either those doors are automatic or Kling couldn’t decide which door she was opening. Kling did an excellent job with the sandwich man. Although, it struggled with keeping the sandwich consistent.

VEO - I was actually surprised at how inaccurate VEO 3.1 was when it came to the door test. It begins well at first. But then, she seems to have had just as much of hard time figuring out how those doors work as I did. The sandwich man test was certainly not what I was expecting. Tony does a great job of informing us how much he is looking forward to the sandwich. However, not only is he already eating something, but he also grabs the sandwich in a way that wouldn’t end well in real life.

Overall, despite both models performing well, I’m gonna have to give the win to Kling 🏆 this round for its consistency and prompt adherence.

- edit the scenes together in iMovie and add simple sfx, music, and transitions.

✔ For the video prompt: A dim room lit only by a soft amber lamp. Dust floats in the air. An old reel-to-reel machine spins slowly, its tape gently wobbling. A faint electrical hum underscores the silence.

Cut to a close-up of a small analog oscilloscope glowing green. The waveform trembles, then sharply stabilizes into two identical spikes—like twin peaks. The machine emits a soft click as its display freezes on a glowing shape: 11.

Camera pans upward to reveal thin trails of rising smoke forming a parallel shape in the lamplight. The room feels suspended in time.

nano banana pro is SO fun 🍌🍌

the model seems to have little restrictions

unfortunately that doesn't translate to Veo tho you can still use Kling 2.5 to animate (i first converted the image to 9:16 ratio)  

my process was simple (prompts included):  

- generated the image, i legit did a super simple prompt:  "show me pokemon #0003 in bladerunner 2049 lighting"  

- then to that image i jsut said "add donald trump to his side, realistic proportions, as if he was his trainer"  

- lastly all i did was convert that to 9:16 with nano banana as well, and asked "add some title as if this was some short movie trailer" 

 - then i animated using kling 2.5 with "High-fidelity cinematic shot. Heavy cyberpunk rainstorm pouring down, raindrops splashing realistically on the wet pavement and bouncing off the Venusaur's skin. Character Motion: Donald Trump and the Venusaur stand stoic and still (idle animation). Subtle breathing movement from the Venusaur's chest and leaves. Trump's trench coat slightly heavy with rain. Background Dynamics: Sci-fi flying cars zooming across the upper sky with light trails. Neon signs flickering and reflecting on the puddles. Steam and volumetric fog rising from the street vents. Camera: Very slow, subtle handheld camera shake to add realism, keeping the focus locked on the duo. 8k resolution, Blade Runner atmosphere."   

- to add sound i went to elevenlabs and added this prompt in the sound effect generator (gave it 20 secs so i had enough space): "Immersive cyberpunk city atmosphere. Occasional, soft, distant 'whooshes' of magnetic levitation cars passing by smoothly. No harsh noises. Ethereal, hypnotic, and cinematic."  

- then i repeated the same to generate the smoke sound, the announcer in the background and the venusaur sounds, 

i was using elevenlabs free and wanted to do it fast, otherwise i would have created a custom female robot announcer voice and use that  

-all i had to do was just stitch things together in a video editor and thats it, IMAGINE WITH PRO EFFORT

prompt: cinematic.text:
The Anatomy of a Perfect AI Prompt: The "Rainbow Finisher" 🌈🤖

​I wanted to push the physics of AI video/image generation to see if I could control the texture of an explosion. Here is the result: A Kaiju hitting a "Rainbow Breath" finisher on a Mech in a cyberpunk city.
​But the image isn't the cool part—the Prompt Engineering is.
​If you are struggling to get dynamic action shots, here is the 3-step logic I used to build this:

​1. The Trigger (Posture)
❌ Don't say: "Monster fighting robot."
✅ I used: "Monster recovering from a punch."
Why: This forces the AI to put the monster low to the ground, creating a desperate, diagonal upward angle for the camera. It builds anticipation.

​2. The Effect (Physics)
❌ Don't say: "Rainbow laser."
✅ I used: "Multicolored rainbow pulse weapon."
Why: Words like "pulse" and "weapon" tell the model this has weight and recoil. It’s not just a light; it’s a physical force.

​3. The Interaction (Texture)
❌ Don't say: " The robot explodes."
✅ I used: "Annihilate into particles."
Why: This is the secret sauce. "Explode" creates a generic fireball. "Annihilate into particles" forces the 'Thanos snap' effect, creating complex debris and dust instead of just fire.
​The result is a clean "Hero Shot" with high contrast and clear action flow.

​Tools: #Gemini #Veo

Style: Cyberpunk / Unreal Engine 5
​#AIArt #PromptEngineering #GenerativeAI #DigitalArt #Cyberpunk #ConceptArt #SYSTEM #CreativeWorkflow #GenAI #Veo3

prompt: cinematic.text:
Kandinsky 5.0: A Family of Foundation Models for Image and Video Generation

- 90% sparse attention (NABLA) → 2.7× faster; VAE 2.5×; sampling steps cut 100→16; 10s 512×768 video in 61s

- Human SBS (MovieGen): >50% preference vs Sora/Veo/Wan; 71% rater consistency

Explained:

Kandinsky 5.0 is an open-source suite of text-conditioned generators for both images and video. It includes Image Lite (6B), Video Lite (2B), and Video Pro (19B), and supports text-to-image, text-to-video, image-to-video, and instruction-based image editing.

At its core is a diffusion transformer (CrossDiT) that fuses visual latents with text features from an LLM. Separate VAEs are used for images (FLUX) and video (HunyuanVideo), helping the models preserve detail in still frames and maintain coherence across time.

A key innovation is NABLA sparse attention. Instead of computing all attention heads, NABLA dynamically turns many off per block, allocating compute to the most useful heads. This yields ~90% sparsity with no measurable loss on standard metrics (CLIP-score, FVD, VBench), enabling a 2.7× speedup.

Training follows a staged pipeline: large-scale pretraining over mixed image/video resolutions; supervised fine-tuning using curated “domain soups” to improve aesthetics and composition; distillation/adversarial post-training to cut diffusion sampling steps (NFE) from 100 to 16; and reward-based fine-tuning (DRaFT) guided by an LLM-initialized reward model.

Data scale and quality control are central: ~500M images and ~250M video scenes are filtered for resolution, deduplication, watermarks, and aesthetics, with multilingual captions and robust edit pairs assembled via CLIP/DINO/face similarity and geometric checks. Human-in-the-loop evaluation is used throughout.

On MovieGen-style human side-by-sides, raters prefer Kandinsky 5.0 outputs over leading closed-source baselines for visual quality, motion, and artifact suppression, with prompt adherence being the main trade-off. Practically, the suite can produce a 10-second 512×768 video in ~61 seconds at 16 sampling steps.

Limitations include a 256-token context in the text encoder (Qwen2.5-VL) and challenges with temporal stability in very long or highly dynamic sequences. Overall, Kandinsky 5.0 advances open-source image/video generation with strong efficiency gains and competitive quality, providing a solid foundation for future multimodal research.

prompt: cinematic.text:
With Veo 3.1, you can now upload multiple reference images alongside your video prompt.
This is HUGE.

Because now, instead of describing your vision endlessly in words, you can show Veo what you mean.

A character from one angle
A background from another
A mood reference
A style reference
A color palette

Even props, costumes, environments.

Veo blends all of them into a single, unified visual language and the output is far more consistent, accurate, and true to your imagination.

🎨 What does this mean for creators?

Simply put, we’re moving one step closer to a world where AI understands vision the same way humans do,  multimodally.

This update allows us to, 

Build entirely new worlds with high fidelity

Maintain consistent characters across shots

Create better continuity in storytelling

Achieve more detailed stylistic control

Reduce trial-and-error with prompting

Save hours of revision time.

For filmmakers, educators, designers, and AI storytellers,  this is a serious upgrade.

💡 Why this matters to me

As someone who experiments with AI video creation almost every day, I often struggle with getting the right look and maintaining character consistency. This single feature solves half of that pain.

Now, instead of fighting the model, we can collaborate with it.

This is not just an update,  it’s a signal.

A signal that Gen AI video tools are evolving rapidly toward real cinematic workflows.

#Google #veo3_1 #veo31 #multimodal

For VEO try adding a line to your prompt that says:
  Music/Sound Effects: ambient sound only.

Some people add a line that says "avoid dialog and music" - but sometimes adding those words in will confuse the model and it will give you (unprompted) dialog and music.

Anatomy of a strong Veo 3 prompt:
Subject • Context • Action • Style • Camera • Composition • Ambiance • Audio

Example:

“A middle-aged man sits alone at a café on a rainy afternoon.
Raindrops streak down the window as reflections of neon signs flicker across his face.
Camera: slow dolly-in through the glass toward him.
Ambiance: cold blue lighting mixed with warm café tones.
Audio: quiet jazz plays, distant thunder rumbles, cups clink softly.”

यह डायलॉग बंदर प्रॉपर लिप्सिंग के साथ हिंदी भाषा में बोलेगा और यह डायलॉग के हिसाब से बंदर हाव-भाव भी करेगा। यही डायलॉग बंदर कैमरे को देखते हुए बोलेगा बाकी नेचुरल आवाज रहेगी वीडियो में और एकदम वीडियो असली दिखेगी।

वीडियो पर किसी भी प्रकार का टेक्स्ट कैप्शन टाइटल नहीं होना चाहिए।

“No cuts. No transitions. No subtitles. No captions. A solitary figure clad in black stands contemplatively, shrouded in shadow, creating a solemn, reflective atmosphere. The camera begins to crane upwards smoothly, moving past the towering columns and pulling forward in a gentle arc that transitions the viewer through the temple’s threshold and into a surreal, cavernous interior. As the camera glides seamlessly inside, the environment shifts to an expansive, fantastical space filled with hovering organic floral spheres and geometric architectural shapes saturated in deep blues, greens, and warm reds. The man’s figure reappears amid this lush, otherworldly garden, now wearing a striking white mask that contrasts against his dark attire. The camera continues a slow dolly-in and gentle pan, emphasizing the intricate textures of the mosaic-like flowers and the interplay of diffuse ambient light that gently illuminates the scene with subtle reflections and shadows. Depth of field softly shifts to highlight the man’s bowed posture and the intricate floating flora as the color palette transitions naturally yet dramatically, preserving a mystical yet contemplative mood throughout the continuous single shot.”

prompt: cinematic.text:
I created this clip with Veo 3.1 fast on Flow. 

My observations:

Flow makes it possible for you to continue your narration with seamless transitions and also allows you to tweak your clips manually for better output quality, but Veo 3.1 has a lot of drawbacks, and it's still some distance from being incorporated into filmmaking.

Weaknesses

- Temporal consistency: The model struggles with scene and temporal consistency and fails to maintain absolute scene settings for each generation. It always modifies or tweaks the scene, character, or physics for each generation, which can affect the naturalness of the footage, making it artificial and less refined.

- Context awareness: In the conclusion of the clip, the princess is running to meet her prince charming, but for some unknown reason, Veo 3.1 kept generating a clip of the prince running from behind to salute the princess. The model should be able to decipher real-world interactions.

- Prompt adherence and physics: The model struggles with executing complex scenes, especially with multiple dialogues, which makes it harder for it because of the 8-second duration. Also, the physics is far from ideal and isn't flawless.

Improvements

I would suggest these improvements:

Veo should be trained to think like a traditional animator—I mean, it should follow the rules of traditional animation when generating clips. Rotoscoping, rigging, etc., should be part of its internal MCP. It should generate the clips in steps and ensure they're near perfect.

Next, prompting can't solve everything; the models need more advanced functionalities. I, for one, would suggest adding an assets library for the models where you can extract objects from generated clips to be saved for future use. For instance, a dress, a room outline, wall decoration, and weather color from a scene can be extracted to be used in another scene.

Also, the model currently allows real-time editing, which can be further improved for physical alignment. For example, if a girl is running in two scenes but the physics are not in tune, there should be a feature to harmonize the physics, background, lighting, etc., to make sure the two scenes blend perfectly.

The video models we currently have allow only two input modes: text-to-video and image-to-video. This greatly limits the models. A video-to-video input has to be integrated into Veo; this will allow it to have more context awareness and reduce bad outputs. The model will be able to analyze its last generation and create footage that will harmonize seamlessly with its last generation. There's also the issue of custom voice integration, which I believe will be added in the future.

Lastly, all video models should have a storyboard—a storyboard where you can input your entire timeline. The model should generate a timeline based on timestamps, with all scene frames consisting of the actions, dialogues, and settings.

This list isn't exhaustive, but I believe with these additions, we will see a massive adoption of AI in Hollywood and the creation of indie movies that are indistinguishable from studio quality. Who knows—maybe the next Christopher Nolan will be a solo AI filmmaker.

@joshwoodward
